sentences.zh: 古里甲石倫

translations.literal: Gulijia Shilun
translations.idiomatic: Gulijia Shilun

sentences.zh: 古里甲石倫，隆安人。

translations.literal: Gulijia Shilun was a native of Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Gulijia Shilun came from Long'an.

sentences.zh: 以武舉登第。

translations.literal: He passed the military examination and gained his degree.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified through the military examination.

sentences.zh: 為人剛悍，頗自用，所在與人不合。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and stubborn; he was rather self-willed, and wherever he served he failed to get along with others.
translations.idiomatic: He was brash and headstrong, inclined to go his own way, and rarely got on with colleagues wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以其勇善戰，每任用之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong, because he was brave and skilled in battle, repeatedly employed him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his courage and skill in warfare, Emperor Xuanzong kept appointing him to active duty.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，累遷副提控、太原府判官，與從宜都提控、振武軍節度使完顏蒲刺都議拒守不合，措置乖方，敵因大入，幾不可禦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou he was promoted in succession to Deputy Ti Control and assistant prefect of Taiyuan; he disagreed with Congyi Metropolitan Ti Control and Zhenwu Army Military Commissioner Wanyan Puluodu over plans to hold off the enemy, their measures were ill-devised, the enemy therefore invaded on a large scale, and they were nearly unable to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 2 he rose stepwise to deputy army controller and Taiyuan assistant prefect; he clashed with Congyi metropolitan controller and Zhenwu commissioner Wanyan Puluodu over how to defend the city, their disorganized arrangements let the enemy pour in, and the position was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 既乃交章論列，以自辨其無罪，上惡其不和，詔分統其兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they exchanged memorials criticizing each other to argue their own innocence; the emperor detested their discord and ordered that their troops be divided for separate command.
translations.idiomatic: They then filed rival memorials blaming each other and pleading innocence; the throne, disgusted by their feud, ordered their forces split between them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷同知太原府事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Associate Administrator of Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made associate prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 奏請招集義軍，設置長校，各立等差。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting to recruit righteous-army militia, establish senior commanders, and set up graded ranks for each.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to raise militia, appoint senior officers, and define a hierarchy of ranks.

sentences.zh: 都統授正七品職，副統正八品，萬戶正九品，千戶正班任使，謀克雜班。

translations.literal: A commander-in-chief was to receive a seventh-rank regular post, a deputy commander an eighth-rank post, a ten-thousand-household chief a ninth-rank post, a thousand-household chief a regular-grade appointment, and a company commander a miscellaneous-grade post.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief were to hold seventh-rank posts, deputy commanders eighth-rank, ten-thousand-household chiefs ninth-rank, thousand-household chiefs regular-grade appointments, and company commanders miscellaneous-grade posts.

sentences.zh: 仍三十人為一謀克，五謀克為一千戶，四千戶為一萬戶，四萬戶為一副統，兩副統為一都統，外設一總領提控。

translations.literal: Moreover, thirty men were to form one company; five companies one thousand-household unit; four thousand households one ten-thousand-household unit; forty thousand households one deputy commander; two deputy commanders one commander-in-chief; and outside this structure one overall supervising Ti Control was to be set up.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty men would form a company, five companies a thousand-household unit, four thousand households a ten-thousand-household unit, forty thousand a deputy command, two deputy commands a full command, with an overall supervising controller above them.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The regulation was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was approved.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，石倫言：「去歲北兵破太原，游兵時入嵐州境，而官民將士悉力捍禦，卒能保守無虞。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year Shilun said: "Last year the northern troops broke Taiyuan; raiding parties sometimes entered Lan Prefecture territory, yet officials, civilians, and soldiers all exerted themselves in defense and in the end were able to hold it secure without mishap.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 Shilun reported: "Last year the northern army took Taiyuan, and raiders kept crossing into Lan Prefecture, yet officials, civilians, and troops threw everything into the defense and the prefecture held without disaster.

sentences.zh: 向者河東內郡，皆駐以精甲，實以資儲，視邊城尤為完富，然兵一至，相繼淪沒。

translations.literal: Formerly the inner commanderies of Hedong were all garrisoned with elite armor and stocked with supplies, regarded as even more complete and rich than border cities, yet once troops arrived they fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The inner Hedong prefectures had once been garrisoned with crack troops and piled with stores—richer, it was thought, than the frontier towns—yet they had fallen in succession as soon as the enemy appeared.

sentences.zh: 嵐兵寡而食不足，惟其上下協同，表裏相應，遂獲安帖。

translations.literal: Lan had few troops and insufficient food, but only because superiors and subordinates cooperated and inner and outer efforts responded to each other did it obtain peace and stability.
translations.idiomatic: Lan had few soldiers and scant grain, yet because leaders and men acted as one and coordinated inside and out, the place stayed secure.

sentences.zh: 當大軍初入，郡縣倉皇，非此帥府控制，則庾、管、保德、岢嵐、寧化皆不可知矣。

translations.literal: When the great army first entered, the prefectures and counties were in panic; had this commandery headquarters not exercised control, the outcome for Yu, Guan, Baode, Kelan, and Ninghua would all have been unknowable.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force first swept in, the districts were in chaos; without control from this headquarters, Yu, Guan, Baode, Kelan, and Ninghua might all have been lost.

sentences.zh: 今防秋不遠，乞朝廷量加旌賞，務令益盡心力，易以鎮守。」

translations.literal: Now the autumn defense is not far off; I beg the court to grant rewards in due measure so that all will exert their hearts and strength the more and find it easier to hold the garrison posts."
translations.idiomatic: Autumn campaigning is near; I ask the court to reward these men proportionately so they will fight harder and hold the line more readily."

sentences.zh: 詔有功者各遷官一級，仍給降空名宣敕，令樞密院遣授之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that those with merit each be promoted one grade in office, and blank appointment commissions were also issued for conferral, with the Bureau of Military Affairs directed to dispatch and award them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered one grade of promotion for each man with merit and issued blank appointment commissions for the Bureau of Military Affairs to distribute.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，石倫奏：「向者並、汾既破，兵入內地，臣謂必攻平陽，平陽不守，將及潞州，其還當由龍州穀以入太原。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Shilun memorialized: "Formerly when Bing and Fen had been broken and troops entered the interior, I said they would surely attack Pingyang; if Pingyang were not held, they would reach Luzhou, and on their return they would enter Taiyuan by way of Longzhou Valley.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 3 Shilun wrote: "After Bing and Fen fell and the enemy pushed inland, I said they would strike Pingyang next; if Pingyang gave way they would reach Luzhou, and on the return march they would come into Taiyuan through Longzhou Valley.

sentences.zh: 故臣嘗請兵欲扼其歸路，朝廷不以為然，既而皆如臣所料。

translations.literal: Therefore I once requested troops to block their line of retreat; the court did not agree, and afterward everything happened as I had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: I had asked for troops to cut off their retreat, but the court disagreed—and events proved me right.

sentences.zh: 始敵入河東時，郡縣民皆攜老幼徙居山險，後雖太原失守，而眾卒不從，其意謂敵不久留，且望官軍複至也。

translations.literal: When the enemy first entered Hedong, the people of the prefectures and counties all took the old and young to dwell in mountain fastnesses; later, though Taiyuan was lost, the masses still did not submit, their idea being that the enemy would not stay long and that they still hoped government troops would return.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy first entered Hedong, county folk moved families into the hills; even after Taiyuan fell the people still held out, expecting a short occupation and the return of imperial troops.

sentences.zh: 今敵居半歲，遣步騎擾諸保聚，而官軍竟無至者，民其能久抗乎。

translations.literal: Now the enemy has been there half a year, sending infantry and cavalry to harass the various fortified settlements, while government troops in the end have not come—how can the people resist for long?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has now been there half a year, raiding every fortified hamlet with infantry and cavalry, while no imperial force has appeared—how long can civilians hold out?

sentences.zh: 夫太原，河東之要郡；

translations.literal: Taiyuan is the vital prefecture of Hedong;
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is the key prefecture of Hedong;

sentences.zh: 平陽，陝西，河南之籓籬也。

translations.literal: Pingyang is the barrier for Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang is the bulwark of Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 若敵兵久不去，居民盡從，屯兵積糧以固基本，而複擾吾郡縣未殘者，則邊城指日皆下矣。

translations.literal: If enemy troops do not leave for long, the inhabitants all follow them, they station troops and store grain to consolidate their base, and again harass our prefectures and counties not yet destroyed, then the border cities will fall within days.
translations.idiomatic: If they stay, win over the population, garrison and stock grain to entrench themselves, and then harry our remaining districts, every border town will fall in short order.

sentences.zh: 北路不守，則南路為邊，去陝西、河南益近，臣竊憂之，故複請兵以圖戰守。

translations.literal: If the northern route is not held, the southern route becomes the frontier, drawing closer to Shaanxi and Henan; I privately worry over this and therefore again request troops to plan for fighting and holding.
translations.idiomatic: If the north cannot be held, the south becomes the front line and Shaanxi and Henan draw nearer to danger; I therefore ask again for troops to fight and defend.

sentences.zh: 而樞府檄臣，並將權太原治中郭遹祖、義軍李天祿等萬餘人，就其糧五千石，會汾州權元帥右都監抹撚胡剌複太原。

translations.literal: But the Bureau of Military Affairs ordered me to take Acting Taiyuan Administrator Guo Yuizu, the righteous-army leader Li Tianlu, and more than ten thousand others, with five thousand shi of their grain, and join Fenzhou Acting Marshal Right Metropolitan Supervisor Monian Hula to recover Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs then ordered me to combine Acting Taiyuan administrator Guo Yuizu, militia leader Li Tianlu, and more than ten thousand men with five thousand shi of grain and rendezvous with Fenzhou acting marshal right metropolitan supervisor Monian Hula to retake Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 臣召遹祖，欲號令其眾，遹祖不從。

translations.literal: I summoned Yuizu intending to command his troops by proclamation; Yuizu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: I summoned Yuizu to take command of his men, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 尋得胡剌報曰：'嘗問軍數于遹祖，但稱天祿等言之，未嘗親閱。

translations.literal: Soon I received Hula's report saying: "I once asked Yuizu about the troop count, but he only said Tianlu and others had spoken of it and had never personally inspected.
translations.idiomatic: Hula soon reported: "When I asked Yuizu for troop numbers he cited what Tianlu and others had said and had never inspected them himself.

sentences.zh: 問糧，則曰散在數處。

translations.literal: When I asked about grain, he said it was scattered in several places.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about grain, he said it was scattered in several places.

sentences.zh: '蓋其情本欲視朝廷以己有兵糧，冀或見用，以取重職，不可指為實用也。

translations.literal: Presumably his intent was originally to show the court that he himself had troops and grain, hoping he might be employed and gain a weighty post; he cannot be pointed to as practically useful.
translations.idiomatic: He plainly wanted the court to think he already had troops and supplies so he might win a major appointment; his forces cannot be relied on in practice.

sentences.zh: 雖然，臣已遣提控石盞吾里忻等領軍以往矣。

translations.literal: Even so, I have already dispatched Ti Control Shizhan Wulixin and others to lead troops there.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, I have already sent controller Shizhan Wulixin and others forward with troops.

sentences.zh: 但敵勢頗重，而往者皆新集白徒，絕無精銳，恐不能勝。

translations.literal: But the enemy's strength is rather heavy, and those sent are all newly gathered raw recruits with absolutely no elite troops; I fear they cannot win.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is strong, however, and the men sent are raw levies without a single crack unit; I fear they will not prevail.

sentences.zh: 乞於河南、陝西量分精兵，以增臣力，仍令陝西州郡近河東者給之資糧，更令南路諸軍綴敵之南，以分其勢，如此庶幾太原可複也。」

translations.literal: I beg that elite troops be allotted in due measure from Henan and Shaanxi to augment my strength, that Shaanxi prefectures and counties near Hedong still be ordered to supply them provisions and grain, and that southern-route armies further tie down the enemy in the south to divide their strength—thus perhaps Taiyuan may be recovered."
translations.idiomatic: I ask for a share of elite troops from Henan and Shaanxi, supplies from Shaanxi districts near Hedong, and southern armies to pin the enemy in the south and divide his strength—only then might Taiyuan be retaken."

sentences.zh: 詔陝西、河東行省分糧與之，請兵之事，以方伐宋不從。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Shaanxi and Hedong Branch Secretariat to divide grain and give it to him; as to the request for troops, because they were then campaigning against Song it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Shaanxi and Hedong branch secretariat to share out grain, but refused the request for troops because a campaign against Song was under way.

sentences.zh: 三月，石倫複上言曰：「頃者大兵破太原，招民耕稼，為久駐之基。

translations.literal: In the third month Shilun again submitted saying: "Recently the great army broke Taiyuan, recruited the people to plow and sow, and laid a foundation for long encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Shilun wrote again: "The enemy has taken Taiyuan, set the people to farming, and is preparing to stay.

sentences.zh: 臣以太原要鎮，所當必爭，遣提控石盞吾里忻引官兵義兵共圖收復。

translations.literal: I regard Taiyuan as a vital strongpoint that must be contested and have dispatched Ti Control Shizhan Wulixin to lead regular troops and righteous-army militia together to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan is a vital post we must fight for; I have sent controller Shizhan Wulixin with regulars and militia to retake it.

sentences.zh: 又以軍士有功者宜速賞之，故擬令吾里忻得注授九品之職，以是請於朝，而執政以為賞功罰罪皆須中覆。

translations.literal: Also, since soldiers with merit ought to be rewarded quickly, I therefore proposed that Wulixin receive appointment to a ninth-rank post and submitted this request to the court, but the chief ministers held that rewarding merit and punishing guilt all require central confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Men with merit should be rewarded at once; I proposed a ninth-rank appointment for Wulixin, but the chief ministers insisted that all rewards and punishments await central approval.

sentences.zh: 夫河東去京師甚遠，移報往返不暇數十日，官軍皆敗亡之餘，鋒銳略盡，而義兵亦不習行陣，無異烏合，以重賞誘之猶恐不為用，況有功而久不見報乎。

translations.literal: Hedong is very far from the capital; memorials going back and forth allow scarcely several tens of days. Government troops are all remnants after defeat and rout, their edge and sharpness nearly exhausted, while the righteous-army militia also do not practice battle formations and are no different from a mob; even with heavy rewards to entice them one still fears they will not serve—how much less when there is merit and reward is long unseen?
translations.idiomatic: Hedong is far from the capital; a round of memorials takes weeks. Our regulars are broken remnants with little fight left, and the militia barely know drill—they are a mob. Heavy rewards may not move them; how will they fight if merit goes unrewarded for months?

sentences.zh: 夫眾不可用則不能退敵，敵不退則太原不可複，太原不可複則平陽之勢日危，而境土日蹙矣。

translations.literal: If the masses cannot be used, the enemy cannot be driven back; if the enemy does not retreat, Taiyuan cannot be recovered; if Taiyuan cannot be recovered, Pingyang's situation grows daily more perilous and the territory daily more constricted.
translations.idiomatic: If these troops will not fight, the enemy will not withdraw; without that, Taiyuan cannot be retaken, Pingyang grows daily more dangerous, and our territory shrinks.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷抑而不許，不過慮其濫賞耳。

translations.literal: Now the court suppresses and does not permit it, nothing more than fearing excessive reward.
translations.idiomatic: The court now refuses only out of fear of over-rewarding.

sentences.zh: 借使有濫賞之弊，其與失太原之害孰重？」

translations.literal: Even supposing there were the abuse of excessive reward, which is heavier—the harm of that or the harm of losing Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if some rewards were excessive, which is worse—that abuse or losing Taiyuan?"

sentences.zh: 於是詔從其請，自太原治中及他州從七品以下職、四品以下散官，並聽石倫遷調焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict granted his request: from Taiyuan Administrator and other prefectures' posts from seventh rank and below, and scattered offices from fourth rank and below, all were to be subject to Shilun's transfer and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then granted his request: Shilun might appoint and transfer Taiyuan administrators and all posts from associate seventh rank down and scattered offices from fourth rank down in other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 是月，石倫複言：「日者遣軍潛搗敵壘，欲分石州兵五百權屯方山，剿殺土寇，且備嵐州，而同知蒲察桓端拒而不發。

translations.literal: That month Shilun again said: "Recently I dispatched troops to strike the enemy camp in secret and wished to detach five hundred Shi Prefecture troops to camp temporarily at Fangshan, suppress and kill local bandits, and also guard Lan Prefecture, but Associate Administrator Pucha Huanduan refused and would not dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: That month Shilun reported: "I had sent men to raid the enemy camp and asked for five hundred Shi Prefecture troops to hold Fangshan, wipe out local bandits, and cover Lan Prefecture, but associate administrator Pucha Huanduan refused to move them.

sentences.zh: 又召同知甯邊軍節度使姚里鴉鶻與之議兵，竟不聽命。

translations.literal: I also summoned Associate Ningbian Army Military Commissioner Yao Li Yagu and discussed troops with him, but in the end he would not obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: I also summoned associate Ningbian commissioner Yao Li Yagu to discuss troop movements, but he ignored my orders.

sentences.zh: 近領兵將取太原，委石州刺史納合萬家權行六部，而辭以他故，幾誤軍糧。

translations.literal: Recently, leading troops to take Taiyuan, I entrusted Shi Prefecture Prefect Nahe Wanjia to act in the Six Ministries' affairs, but he declined on other grounds and nearly caused army grain to go wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When I recently marched to retake Taiyuan I left Shi prefect Nahe Wanjia acting for the six ministries; he pleaded other business and nearly ruined the army's grain supply.

sentences.zh: 約武州刺史郭憲率所領並進，憲亦不至。

translations.literal: I arranged for Wu Prefecture Prefect Guo Xian to lead his command and advance together; Xian also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: I had arranged for Wu prefect Guo Xian to advance with his command, but he too failed to appear.

sentences.zh: 臣猥當方面之任，而所統官屬並不稟從，乞朝廷嚴為懲誡，庶人知職分，易以責辦。」

translations.literal: I unworthily hold a regional commission, yet the officials I command all fail to obey instructions; I beg the court to punish them severely so that men may know their duties and it may be easier to hold them accountable."
translations.idiomatic: I hold a regional command, yet my subordinates will not obey; I ask the court to punish them severely so men know their duty and I can enforce my orders."

sentences.zh: 宰臣惡之，乃奏曰：「桓端、鴉鶻已經奏改，無複可議。

translations.literal: The chief ministers disliked this and memorialized: "Huanduan and Yagu have already been memorialized for transfer; there is nothing further to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, displeased, replied: "Huanduan and Yagu have already been transferred by memorial; there is nothing more to debate.

sentences.zh: 石倫身兼行部，不自規畫，而使萬家往來應給，石州無人，恐亦有失。

translations.literal: Shilun himself concurrently holds touring ministry duties yet does not plan on his own and instead has Wanjia go back and forth to supply needs; with no one in Shi Prefecture, I fear there may also be loss.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun himself holds touring ministry duties yet does not plan them and sends Wanjia back and forth on supply errands, leaving Shi Prefecture empty—another mistake, surely.

sentences.zh: 武州邊郡，正當兵沖，使憲率軍離城，敵或乘之，孰與守禦？

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture is a border commandery right in the path of troops; if Xian is made to lead his army away from the city and the enemy seizes the chance, who is to defend?
translations.idiomatic: Wu is a frontier prefecture in the path of invasion; if Xian marches away, who will hold the city when the enemy strikes?

sentences.zh: 萬家等不從，未為過也。」

translations.literal: That Wanjia and others did not obey is not yet a fault."
translations.idiomatic: Wanjia and the others were not at fault in refusing."

sentences.zh: 上以為然，因遣諭石倫曰：「卿嘗行院於歸德，衛州防備之事，非不素知，乃屢以步騎為請何耶？

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct and therefore sent instructions to Shilun saying: "You once conducted the touring commission at Guide; you are not unacquainted with Weizhou's defense affairs—why then do you repeatedly request infantry and cavalry?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Shilun word: "You once ran the touring commission at Guide and know Weizhou's defenses well—why do you keep asking for infantry and cavalry?

sentences.zh: 比授卿三品，且數免罪譴卿，嘗自誓以死報國，今所為如此，豈報國之道哉！

translations.literal: Recently you were granted third rank and several times pardoned from punishment; you once vowed yourself to repay the state with death—yet your conduct now is such; is this the way to repay the state!
translations.idiomatic: You were lately raised to third rank and repeatedly pardoned; you once swore to die for the state—yet you act like this. Is that how one serves the country?

sentences.zh: 意謂河南之眾必不可分，但圖他日得以藉口耳。

translations.literal: Your idea is surely that Henan's forces absolutely cannot be divided and you only plan to have an excuse on some future day.
translations.idiomatic: You surely know Henan's troops cannot be split and only want an excuse for later.

sentences.zh: 卿果赤必為國，盡力經畫，亦足自效。

translations.literal: If you are truly utterly loyal and act for the state, exert your strength in planning and that too is enough to prove yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you are truly loyal, throw yourself into planning and you will still prove your worth.

sentences.zh: 萬家等若必懲戒，彼中誰複可使者？

translations.literal: If Wanjia and others must be punished, who there can again be sent into service?
translations.idiomatic: If you punish Wanjia and the rest, who in that region will still serve you?

sentences.zh: 姑為容忍可也。」

translations.literal: For the present, tolerance will do."
translations.idiomatic: For now, bear with them."

sentences.zh: 閏三月，石倫駐兵太原之西，俟諸道兵至進戰，聞脅從人頗有革心，上言於朝，乞降空名宣敕、金銀符，許便宜遷注，以招誘之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month Shilun stationed troops west of Taiyuan, waiting for armies from the various routes to arrive before advancing to battle; hearing that those coerced to follow the enemy were quite inclined to change heart, he submitted to the court requesting blank appointment commissions and gold-and-silver tallies, with permission for discretionary appointment and registration to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month Shilun camped west of Taiyuan awaiting reinforcements; learning that many who had followed the enemy were wavering, he asked the court for blank commissions and gold-and-silver tallies with authority to appoint men on the spot and win them over.

sentences.zh: 上從其請，並給付之，仍聽注五品以下官職。

translations.literal: The emperor granted his request, gave them all to him, and still permitted appointment to offices of fifth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, issued them, and allowed him to appoint offices up to fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 六月，保德州振威軍萬戶王章、弩軍萬戶齊鎮殺其刺史孛術魯銀術哥，仍滅其家，脅官吏軍民同狀白嵐州帥府，言銀術哥專恣慘酷，私造甲仗，將謀不軌。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Baode Prefecture Zhenwu Army Ten-Thousand-Household Chief Wang Zhang and Crossbow Army Ten-Thousand-Household Chief Qi Zhen killed their prefect Boshulu Yinshuge, and still exterminated his household, coercing officials, soldiers, and civilians to submit a joint report to the Lan Prefecture command headquarters saying Yinshuge was willful and cruel, privately made armor and weapons, and was about to plot sedition.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Baode Zhenwu Army commander Wang Zhang and crossbow-army commander Qi Zhen murdered their prefect Boshulu Yinshuge and wiped out his family, then forced officials, troops, and civilians to sign a joint report to the Lan headquarters accusing Yinshuge of tyranny, secretly forging arms, and plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 石倫密令同知州事把蒲剌都圖之，蒲剌都乃與兵吏置酒召章等欽，擒而族誅之。

translations.literal: Shilun secretly ordered Associate Prefect Ba Puluodu to plot against them; Puluodu then with military clerks set out wine and summoned Zhang and others to drink, seized them, and executed their clans.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun secretly ordered associate prefect Ba Puluodu to deal with them; Puluodu gave a banquet for Zhang and his fellows, seized them, and executed their entire families.

sentences.zh: 至是，朝廷命行省胥鼎量宜遷賞，仍令蒲剌都攝州事，撫安其眾焉。

translations.literal: At this time the court ordered Branch Secretariat Xudding to grant promotions and rewards as appropriate, and still ordered Puluodu to act in prefectural affairs and pacify the masses.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered branch secretariat Xudding to reward men as he saw fit and left Puluodu acting prefect to calm the people.

sentences.zh: 正大八年，大兵入河南，州郡無不下者，朝議以權昌武軍節度使粘葛仝周不知兵事，起石倫代之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhengda the great army entered Henan and there was no prefecture or commandery that did not fall; the court discussed that Acting Changwu Army Military Commissioner Niange Tongzhou did not understand military affairs and raised Shilun to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengda 8 the main army swept into Henan and every prefecture fell; the court decided that acting Changwu commissioner Niange Tongzhou was no soldier and recalled Shilun to replace him.

sentences.zh: 石倫初赴昌武，詔諭曰：「卿先朝宿將，甚有威望，故起拜是職。

translations.literal: When Shilun first went to Changwu, an edict instructed him: "You are a veteran general of the former reign with great prestige; therefore you are raised and appointed to this post.
translations.idiomatic: As Shilun set out for Changwu, an edict told him: "You are a seasoned general of the previous reign with great standing; that is why you are called back to this post.

sentences.zh: 元帥蘇椿、武監軍皆曉兵事，今在昌武，宜與同議，勿複不睦失計也。」

translations.literal: Marshals Su Chun and the Wu Military Supervisor all understand military affairs and are now at Changwu; you should deliberate together and not again be at odds and lose your plans."
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Su Chun and the Wu military supervisor both know warfare and are at Changwu; consult with them and do not quarrel again to the ruin of your plans."

sentences.zh: 時北兵已至許，石倫赴鎮，幾為遊騎所獲。

translations.literal: At that time the northern troops had already reached Xu; Shilun went to his commission and was nearly captured by raiding horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army had already reached Xu when Shilun took up his post and was nearly caught by raiders.

sentences.zh: 數日，知兩省軍敗，潰軍踵來。

translations.literal: Within several days he learned that the armies of the two branch secretariats had been defeated and routed troops came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he learned that the armies of both branch secretariats had been beaten and broken troops kept streaming in.

sentences.zh: 有忠孝軍完顏副統入城，兩手皆折，血污滿身，州人憂怖不知所出。

translations.literal: A Zhongxiao Army Wanyan deputy commander entered the city with both hands broken, his body covered in blood and filth; the people of the prefecture were anxious and terrified, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: A Zhongxiao Army Wanyan deputy commander came into the city with both arms broken and covered in blood; the townspeople were terrified and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 石倫遣歸順軍提控嵐州人高珪往斥候，珪因持在州軍馬糧草數目奔大元軍，仍告以城池深淺。

translations.literal: Shilun dispatched Guishun Army Ti Control Gao Gui, a native of Lan Prefecture, to reconnoiter; Gui thereupon took the counts of troops, horses, and grain in the prefecture and fled to the Great Yuan army, still informing them of the depth and shallowness of the city's defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun sent Guishun Army controller Gao Gui of Lan Prefecture to scout; Gui fled to the Great Yuan army with tallies of the city's troops, horses, and grain and told them how strong or weak the defenses were.

sentences.zh: 俄大兵至城下，以鳳翔府韓壽孫持檄招降，言三峰敗狀。

translations.literal: Soon the great army reached below the city walls; Fengxiang Prefecture's Han Shousun bore a proclamation to summon surrender and spoke of the defeat at Sanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main force was at the walls; Han Shousun of Fengxiang came with a summons to surrender and described the rout at Sanfeng.

sentences.zh: 石倫、蘇椿不詰問即斬之市中。

translations.literal: Shilun and Su Chun did not interrogate him but immediately executed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun and Su Chun had him beheaded in the market without a hearing.

sentences.zh: 既而武監軍偏裨何魏輩開東門，內族按春開南門，夾谷太守開西門。

translations.literal: Before long Wu Military Supervisor's junior officers He Wei and others opened the east gate, imperial clansman An Chun opened the south gate, and Jiagu the prefect opened the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: Then Wu military supervisor's lieutenants He Wei and others opened the east gate, imperial clansman An Chun the south gate, and prefect Jiagu the west gate.

sentences.zh: 大元軍入城，擒蘇椿，問以大名南奔之事，椿曰：「我本金朝人，無力故降，我歸國得為大官，何謂反耶！」

translations.literal: The Great Yuan army entered the city, seized Su Chun, and questioned him about fleeing south from Daming; Chun said: "I was originally a man of the Jin dynasty; because I had no strength I therefore surrendered. If I return to my state I can become a great official—how can you call it rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: The Great Yuan troops entered, seized Su Chun, and asked about his flight south from Daming; Chun said: "I am a Jin subject who surrendered from weakness; if I return home I shall hold high office—how is that rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 大將怒其不屈，即殺之。

translations.literal: The general was angry at his refusal to submit and immediately killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The commander, enraged by his defiance, killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 石倫投廨後井中，仝周自縊州廨。

translations.literal: Shilun threw himself into the well behind the government offices; Tongzhou hanged himself in the prefectural offices.
translations.idiomatic: Shilun threw himself into the well behind the yamen; Tongzhou hanged himself in the prefectural hall.

sentences.zh: 武監軍者初不預開門之謀，何魏輩欲保全之，故言于大將曰：「監軍令我輩獻門。」

translations.literal: The Wu Military Supervisor at first had not taken part in the plan to open the gates; He Wei and the others wished to preserve him and therefore said to the general: "The military supervisor ordered us to present the gate."
translations.idiomatic: The Wu military supervisor had not been in the plot to open the gates; He Wei and his men tried to save him and told the commander: "The military supervisor ordered us to open the gate."

sentences.zh: 然亦怒其不迎軍而降，亦殺之。

translations.literal: Yet they were also angry that he had not welcomed the army and surrendered, and they killed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: But they were still angry that he had not come out to welcome the army and surrender, and killed him too.

sentences.zh: 仝周名暉，字子陽，策論進士，興定間為徐州行樞密院參議官，上章言：「惟名與器不可假人，自古帝王靡不為重。

translations.literal: Tongzhou's name was Hui, style Ziyang, a Policy Treatise advanced scholar; during Xingding he was a participating officer of the Xuzhou Touring Bureau of Military Affairs and submitted a memorial saying: "Titles and regalia must not be lent to others; from antiquity emperors and kings have all held this weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Tongzhou, personal name Hui, style Ziyang, had passed the policy-treatise examination; in the Xingding era he was a participating officer of the Xuzhou touring bureau of military affairs and wrote: "Rank and regalia must not be lent lightly; every dynasty has treated them as sacred.

sentences.zh: 今之金銀牌，即古符節也，其上有太祖禦畫，往年得佩者甚難，兵興以來授予頗濫，市井道路黃白相望，恐非所以示信於下也。

translations.literal: Today's gold and silver tallies are the ancient tallies of authority; upon them is the Taizu's imperial painting. In former years those who obtained them to wear were very few; since warfare arose grants have been rather excessive, and in market streets and on the roads gold and silver gleam facing each other—I fear this is not the way to show trust to those below.
translations.idiomatic: Today's gold and silver tallies are the old credentials of command, bearing the Taizu's own brushwork. Once they were rarely bestowed; since the wars began they have been handed out freely until markets and roads glitter with them—I fear that no longer inspires trust below.

sentences.zh: 乞寶惜之，有所甄別。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be treasured and that there be discrimination in granting them."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be treasured and granted with discrimination."

sentences.zh: 上以語宰臣，而丞相高琪等奏：「時方多難，急於用人，駕馭之方，此其一也，如故為便。」

translations.literal: The emperor spoke of this to the chief ministers, and Chancellor Gao Qi and others memorialized: "The time is full of many difficulties and there is urgency in employing men; methods of controlling them—this is one—and to keep the former practice is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mentioned this to his ministers; Chancellor Gao Qi and others replied: "These are desperate times and men are needed at once; loosening credentials is one way to command them, and the old practice should stand."

sentences.zh: 蘇椿，大名人，初守大名，歸順於大元，正大二年九月，自大名奔汴，詔置許州，至是，見殺。

translations.literal: Su Chun was a native of Daming; he first defended Daming and submitted to Great Yuan; in the ninth month of the second year of Zhengda he fled from Daming to Bian and was ordered posted at Xu Prefecture; at this time he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chun came from Daming; he had first held Daming, then submitted to Great Yuan; in the ninth month of Zhengda 2 he fled from Daming to Bian and was posted at Xu Prefecture; now he was killed.

sentences.zh: 完顏訛可

translations.literal: Wanyan Eke
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Eke

sentences.zh: 完顏訛可，內族也。

translations.literal: Wanyan Eke was of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Eke was of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 時有兩訛可，皆護衛出身，一曰「草火訛可」，每得賊，好以草火燎之，一曰「板子訛可」，嘗誤以宮中牙牌報班齊者為板子，故時人各以是目之。

translations.literal: At the time there were two Ekes, both from the guards corps; one was called "Straw-Fire Eke," who whenever he captured bandits liked to burn them with straw fire, and one was called "Board Eke," who once mistook the palace ivory tallies used to report that the shift was assembled for boards—therefore people of the time each viewed them by these names.
translations.idiomatic: There were two men named Eke, both from the guards: one was called "Straw-Fire Eke" because he liked to burn captives with straw torches, the other "Board Eke" because he once mistook the palace tally boards that announced the watch for wooden planks—hence their nicknames.

sentences.zh: 正大八年九月，大兵攻河中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Zhengda the great army attacked Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Zhengda 8 the main army attacked Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗議遷都，朝臣謂可遷河中：「河中背負關陝五路，士馬全盛，南阻大河，可建行台以為右翼。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Xuanzong discussed moving the capital, court ministers said the capital could be moved to Hezhong: "Hezhong backs upon the five circuits of Guan and Shaan with troops and horses in full strength; to the south the great river blocks the way; a touring office can be established as the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong first debated moving the capital, some ministers urged Hezhong: "Hezhong rests on the five Guan-Shaan circuits with full armies and horses, is barred to the south by the Yellow River, and could host a touring office as the right wing.

sentences.zh: 前有絳陽、平陽、太原三大鎮，敵兵不敢輕入。

translations.literal: Before it are the three great strongpoints Jiangyang, Pingyang, and Taiyuan; enemy troops would not dare enter lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyang, Pingyang, and Taiyuan stand before it as three great bastions, so the enemy would not advance lightly.

sentences.zh: 應三鎮郡縣之民皆聚之山寨，敵至則為晝攻夜劫之計。

translations.literal: The people of the prefectures and counties answering to the three strongpoints should all gather in mountain stockades; when the enemy arrives they can employ the plan of attacking by day and raiding by night.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the districts under those three bastions should gather in mountain stockades and, when the enemy comes, harass him by day and raid by night.

sentences.zh: 屯重軍中條，則行在有萬全之固矣。」

translations.literal: Station heavy troops at Zhongtiao and the mobile court will have a defense of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: With heavy troops at Zhongtiao, the mobile court would be perfectly secure."

sentences.zh: 主議者以河中在河朔，又無宮室，不及汴梁，議遂寢。

translations.literal: Those leading the discussion held that Hezhong was in the north of the river, moreover had no palaces, and did not equal Bianliang; the discussion therefore lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The advocates of the plan replied that Hezhong lay north of the river, lacked palace buildings, and could not rival Bianliang, and the proposal died.

sentences.zh: 宣宗既遷河南，三二年之後，詔元帥都監內族阿祿帶行帥府事。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanzong had moved to Henan, two or three years later he ordered Marshal Metropolitan Supervisor imperial clansman Aludai to conduct marshalate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanzong moved to Henan, two or three years later he ordered imperial clansman Aludai, metropolitan supervisor of the marshalate, to run the commandery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 阿祿帶恇怯不能軍，竭民膏血為浚築之計。

translations.literal: Aludai was timid and cowardly and could not command troops, draining the people's fat and blood for dredging and construction plans.
translations.idiomatic: Aludai was timid and useless in the field, draining the people dry for digging and building works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，絳州破，阿祿帶益懼，馳奏河中孤城不可守。

translations.literal: Before long Jiang Prefecture was broken; Aludai grew still more afraid and urgently memorialized that the isolated city of Hezhong could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiang Prefecture fell; Aludai grew more frightened and urgently reported that isolated Hezhong could not be held.

sentences.zh: 有旨親視，果不可守則棄之，無至資敵。

translations.literal: There was an order to inspect in person; if it truly could not be held then abandon it, and do not go so far as to supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to inspect in person; if the city truly could not be held he might abandon it, but not enrich the enemy.

sentences.zh: 阿祿帶遂棄河中，燒民戶官府，一二日而盡。

translations.literal: Aludai thereupon abandoned Hezhong, burning civilian households and government offices, and in a day or two all was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Aludai then abandoned Hezhong, burning homes and government buildings until nothing was left within a day or two.

sentences.zh: 尋有言河中重鎮，國家基本所在，棄之為失策，設為敵人所據，則大河之險我不得專恃矣。

translations.literal: Soon there were those who said Hezhong was a vital strongpoint where the state's foundation lay; to abandon it was a mistaken policy—supposing the enemy held it, then the great river's defenses we could not rely on exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Soon critics said Hezhong was a vital post and the foundation of the state; abandoning it was a blunder, for if the enemy held it the Jin could no longer rely on the Yellow River alone.

sentences.zh: 宣宗悔悟，系阿祿帶同州獄，累命完複之，隨守隨破。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong repented and understood; he imprisoned Aludai in Tong Prefecture's jail and repeatedly ordered complete recovery of it, but as soon as it was held it was broken.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong came to his senses, imprisoned Aludai in Tong Prefecture, and repeatedly ordered Hezhong retaken, but it fell as soon as it was garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 至是，以內族兩訛可將兵三萬守之。

translations.literal: At this time the two imperial-clan Ekes were ordered to command thirty thousand troops to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Now the two imperial-clan Ekes were sent with thirty thousand men to hold it.

sentences.zh: 大兵謀取宋武休關。

translations.literal: The great army planned to take Song's Wuxiu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The main army aimed to seize the Song fortress at Wuxiu Pass.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鳳翔破，睿宗分騎兵三萬入散關，攻破鳳州，徑過華陽，屠洋州，攻武休關。

translations.literal: Before long Fengxiang was broken; Ruizong divided thirty thousand cavalry to enter San Pass, broke Feng Prefecture, passed straight through Huayang, slaughtered Yang Prefecture, and attacked Wuxiu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Fengxiang fell; Ruizong sent thirty thousand horsemen through San Pass, took Feng Prefecture, marched through Huayang, massacred Yang Prefecture, and assaulted Wuxiu Pass.

sentences.zh: 開生山，截焦崖，出武休東南，遂圍興元。

translations.literal: They opened Sheng Mountain, cut Jiao Cliff, emerged southeast of Wuxiu, and thereupon besieged Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: They cut roads through Sheng Mountain and Jiao Cliff, came out southeast of Wuxiu, and besieged Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 興元軍民散走，死于沙窩者數十萬。

translations.literal: The soldiers and civilians of Xingyuan scattered and fled; those who died in Shawan numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians of Xingyuan fled in panic; several hundred thousand died at Shawan.

sentences.zh: 分軍而西，西軍由別路入沔州，取大安軍路開魚鱉山，撤屋為筏，渡嘉陵江入關堡，並江趨葭萌，略地至西水縣而還。

translations.literal: The army divided and went west; the western army by a separate route entered Mian Prefecture, took the Da'an Army route to open Yubie Mountain, tore down houses to make rafts, crossed the Jialing River into pass fortresses, followed the river toward Jiameng, raided territory as far as Xishui County, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The force split westward: the western column entered Mian by another route, opened Yubie Mountain on the Da'an Army road, tore down houses for rafts, crossed the Jialing into the pass forts, followed the river to Jiameng, raided as far as Xishui County, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 東軍止屯興元、洋州之間，遂趨饒峰。

translations.literal: The eastern army only encamped between Xingyuan and Yang Prefecture, then hastened toward Raofeng.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern column camped between Xingyuan and Yang Prefecture, then marched on Raofeng.

sentences.zh: 宋人棄關不守，大兵乃得入。

translations.literal: The Song people abandoned the passes and did not defend them, and the great army was thereby able to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Song abandoned the passes undefended, and the main army poured through.

sentences.zh: 初，大兵期以明年正月合南北軍攻汴梁，故自將攻河中。

translations.literal: Earlier the great army had scheduled the first month of the coming year for northern and southern armies to unite and attack Bianliang; therefore he personally led the attack on Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The main army had planned a joint north-south assault on Bianliang in the first month of the coming year; the commander therefore led the Hezhong campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 河中告急，合打蒲阿遣王敢率步兵一萬救之。

translations.literal: Hezhong reported urgent distress; Heda Pu'a dispatched Wang Gan leading ten thousand infantry to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong sent desperate appeals; Heda Pu'a dispatched Wang Gan with ten thousand foot soldiers to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 十二月，河中破。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Hezhong was broken.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Hezhong fell.

sentences.zh: 初，河中主將知大兵將至，懼軍力不足，截故城 之半守之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Hezhong commander, knowing the great army was about to arrive and fearing insufficient military strength, cut off half the old city to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The Hezhong commander, expecting the main army and fearing he had too few men, walled off only half the old city for defense.

sentences.zh: 及被攻，行帳命築松樓高二百尺，下瞰城中，土山地穴百道並進。

translations.literal: When it was attacked, the field headquarters ordered pine towers two hundred feet high built to look down into the city; earthen mounds and underground tunnels advanced by a hundred routes together.
translations.idiomatic: Under assault, the field headquarters built two-hundred-foot pine towers overlooking the city and pressed the siege with earthen mounds and tunnels on every side.

sentences.zh: 至十一月，攻愈急。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month the attack grew still more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month the assault had intensified.

sentences.zh: 自王敢救軍至，軍士殊死鬥，日夜不休，西北樓櫓俱盡，白戰又半月，力盡乃陷。

translations.literal: From the time Wang Gan's relief army arrived, the soldiers fought to the death without rest day or night; the northwest towers and parapets were all destroyed, hand-to-hand fighting continued another half month, and when strength was exhausted it fell.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Gan's relief force arrived the garrison fought day and night without rest; the northwest towers were smashed, hand-to-hand combat lasted another fortnight, and the city fell only when strength was spent.

sentences.zh: 草訛可戰數十合始被擒，尋殺之。

translations.literal: Straw-Fire Eke fought several tens of engagements before he was captured at last, and soon they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Straw-Fire Eke fought dozens of engagements before he was taken and soon executed.

sentences.zh: 板訛可提敗卒三千奪船走，北兵追及，鼓噪北岸上，矢石如雨。

translations.literal: Board Eke led three thousand defeated troops to seize boats and flee; the northern troops overtook them, drumming and shouting on the north bank, arrows and stones like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Board Eke gathered three thousand survivors, seized boats, and fled; northern troops caught up on the north bank amid drums and shouts, arrows and stones falling like rain.

sentences.zh: 數里之外有戰船橫截之，敗軍不得過，船中有齎火砲名「震天雷」者連發之，砲火明，見北船軍無幾人，力斫橫船開，得至潼關，遂入閿鄉。

translations.literal: Several li away warships lay across to block them; the defeated army could not pass. On the ships were men carrying fire-projectors called "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" that fired in succession; when the cannon fire lit up, they saw few northern troops on the boats, exerted force to chop through the blocking ships and open a way, reached Tong Pass, and then entered Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: A few li downstream warships barred their path. Enemy vessels fired "Heaven-Shaking Thunder" incendiary bombs in succession; in the flashes Board Eke saw few men aboard, hacked through the blockade, reached Tong Pass, and escaped into Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 尋有詔赦將佐以下，責訛可以不能死，車載入陝州，決杖二百。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict pardoning commanders and assistants below; Eke was blamed for not being able to die, loaded on a cart into Shaan Prefecture, and given two hundred strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon pardoned the officers and men but blamed Eke for failing to die fighting; he was carted to Shaan Prefecture and beaten with the staff two hundred times.

sentences.zh: 識者以為河中城守不下，德順力竭而陷，非戰之罪，故訛可之死，人有冤之者。

translations.literal: Those with insight held that Hezhong's defense could not be taken down, that it fell because virtue and obedience were exhausted, not because of guilt in battle; therefore in Eke's death some considered him wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledgeable men said Hezhong had held out until strength was spent, not through cowardice in battle, and that Eke's punishment was unjust.

sentences.zh: 初，訛可以元帥右監軍、邠涇總帥、權參知知事，奉旨於邠、涇、鳳翔往來防秋。

translations.literal: Earlier Eke held the posts of Marshal Right Metropolitan Supervisor, Bin-Jing Commander-in-Chief, and Acting Participating Administrator; by imperial order he went back and forth among Bin, Jing, and Fengxiang for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Eke had been marshal right metropolitan supervisor, Bin-Jing commander-in-chief, and acting participating administrator, ordered to patrol Bin, Jing, and Fengxiang on autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 奉禦六兒監戰，於訛可為孫行，而訛可動為所制，意頗不平，漸生猜隙。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu'er supervised the campaign and ranked as Eke's grandson in precedence, yet Eke was constantly controlled by him, his mind quite resentful, and suspicion and rifts gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Liu'er served as battle supervisor and outranked Eke; Eke resented his constant interference and suspicion grew between them.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，召赴京師，改河中總帥，受京兆節制。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year he was summoned to the capital, changed to Hezhong Commander-in-Chief, and placed under Jingzhao's control.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 7 he was recalled to the capital, made Hezhong commander-in-chief, and placed under Jingzhao's authority.

sentences.zh: 此時六兒同赴召，謂訛可奉旨往來防秋，而乃畏怯避遠，正與朝旨相違，上意頗罪訛可。

translations.literal: At this time Liu'er went to the summons together with him, saying Eke had been ordered to go back and forth on autumn defense yet was timid and kept far away, exactly contrary to the court's intent; the emperor's mind quite blamed Eke.
translations.idiomatic: Liu'er went to court with him and accused Eke of shirking the autumn-defense duties he had been assigned; the emperor was much displeased with Eke.

sentences.zh: 及河中陷，苦戰力盡，而北兵百倍臨之，人謂雖至不守猶可以自贖，竟杖而死，蓋六兒先入之言主之也。

translations.literal: When Hezhong fell, after bitter fighting and exhausted strength, with northern troops a hundredfold upon them, people said that even if it could not be held one might still redeem oneself—yet in the end he was beaten to death, probably because Liu'er's earlier words held sway.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhong fell after a desperate defense against overwhelming northern forces, many said Eke deserved redemption even in defeat; he was beaten to death instead, largely because Liu'er's earlier accusations had already swayed the court.

sentences.zh: 劉祁曰：「金人南渡之後，近侍之權尤重。

translations.literal: Liu Qi said: "After the Jin people crossed south, the power of close attendants was especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi wrote: "After the Jin crossed the river southward, the power of palace attendants grew especially heavy.

sentences.zh: 蓋宣宗喜用其人以為耳目，伺察百官，故奉禦輩採訪民間，號'行路禦史'，或得一二事即入奏之，上因以責台官漏泄，皆抵罪。

translations.literal: Because Emperor Xuanzong liked to use such men as his eyes and ears to spy on the hundred officials, therefore the palace attendants investigated among the people and were called 'roadside censors'; if they obtained one or two matters they at once entered and reported them, and the emperor thereby blamed the censorate officials for leaks—all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong used them as spies on the bureaucracy, so attendants prowled the streets as 'roadside censors' and reported whatever they heard; the emperor then punished the regular censors for leaking secrets.

sentences.zh: 又方面之柄雖委將帥，又差一奉禦在軍中，號曰'監戰'，每臨機制變，多為所牽制，遇敵輒先奔，故師多喪敗。」

translations.literal: Moreover, though regional authority was entrusted to generals, another palace attendant was also dispatched in the army, called 'battle supervisor'; whenever critical decisions arose they were mostly constrained by him; meeting the enemy they would flee first—therefore armies often suffered defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Though field command was given to generals, an attendant was also sent with each army as 'battle supervisor,' constraining every decision; at contact with the enemy he often fled first, and armies were repeatedly ruined."

sentences.zh: 哀宗因之不改，終至亡國。

translations.literal: Emperor Aizong followed this without change and in the end reached the loss of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Aizong left the practice unchanged, and the dynasty perished.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古里甲石倫善戰而好犯法，故見廢者屢，晚起為將，卒死於難。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Gulijia Shilun was skilled in battle yet fond of breaking the law; therefore he was repeatedly dismissed. Raised late as a general, he finally died in calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Gulijia Shilun fought well but loved to break the law, was repeatedly dismissed, was raised late as a general, and died in the final catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 金運將終，又用數奇之李廣，其乏絕不亦宜乎。

translations.literal: As Jin's fortune was about to end, they again employed a Li Guang of unlucky number—was it not fitting that supplies ran out?
translations.idiomatic: As Jin's fate neared its end they again relied on a Li Guang of ill-starred campaigns—small wonder their resources gave out.

sentences.zh: 草訛可力戰而死，板訛可亦力戰，不死於陣而死于刑，論者以為有近侍先入之言。

translations.literal: Straw-Fire Eke fought hard and died; Board Eke also fought hard, not dying on the battlefield but dying under punishment—commentators held that there were prior words from close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Straw-Fire Eke died fighting; Board Eke fought equally hard but died under the rod, not in battle—commentators blamed the prior accusations of palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 夫以褻禦治軍，既掣之肘，又信其讒以殺人，金失政刑矣。

translations.literal: To govern armies with intimate attendants, both restraining the elbow and trusting their slander to kill men—the Jin had lost proper government and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: To run armies through intimate attendants who hamstrung commanders and whose slander brought executions was to abandon government and justice altogether.

sentences.zh: 唐之亡，坐以近侍監軍，金蹈其轍，哀哉。

translations.literal: Tang's fall sat upon close attendants supervising armies; Jin followed in their tracks—alas.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had fallen because intimate attendants supervised armies; Jin followed the same road—alas.

sentences.zh: 撒合輦

translations.literal: Sa Henian
translations.idiomatic: Sa Henian

sentences.zh: 四年，大元既滅西夏，進軍陝西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, after Great Yuan had already destroyed Western Xia, they advanced into Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, after Great Yuan destroyed Western Xia, its armies advanced into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 四月丙申，召尚書溫蒂罕壽孫、中丞烏古孫卜吉、祭酒裴滿阿虎帶、直學士蒲察世達、右司諫陳規、監察烏古論四和完顏習顯、同判睦親府事撒合輦同議西事，上曰：「已諭合達盡力決一戰矣。」

translations.literal: On bingchen of the fourth month the emperor summoned Minister Wentihen Shousun, Censor-in-Chief Wugusun Buji, Libationer Peiman Ahudai, Academician Pucha Shida, Right Remonstrance Officer Chen Gui, Investigators Wugulun Sihe and Wanyan Xixian, and Associate Administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin Sa Henian to deliberate together on western affairs; the emperor said: "I have already instructed Heda to exert his strength and settle the issue in one battle."
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of the fourth month the emperor summoned Minister Wentihen Shousun, censor-in-chief Wugusun Buji, libationer Peiman Ahudai, academician Pucha Shida, remonstrance officer Chen Gui, investigators Wugulun Sihe and Wanyan Xixian, and associate administrator of the Office of Imperial Kin Sa Henian to discuss the western front. The emperor said: "I have already ordered Heda to stake everything on one decisive battle."

sentences.zh: 群臣多主和事，獨輦力破和議，語在《陳規傳》。

translations.literal: Most of the ministers favored peace; Henian alone forcefully broke the peace proposal—the account is in the Biography of Chen Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Most ministers favored peace; only Henian forcefully blocked the peace proposal, as told in the biography of Chen Gui.

sentences.zh: 八月，朝廷得清水之報，令有司罷防城及修城丁壯，凡軍需租調不急者權停。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the court received reports from Qingshui and ordered the relevant offices to dismiss men for city defense and wall repair, and to suspend temporarily all military supplies, rents, and levies that were not urgent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month reports from Qingshui reached the court; officials were ordered to release men from garrison and wall work and to suspend non-urgent military levies and taxes.

sentences.zh: 初，聞大兵自鳳翔入京兆，關中大震，以中丞卜吉、祭酒阿忽帶兼司農卿，簽民兵，督秋稅，令民入保為避遷計。

translations.literal: Earlier, hearing that the great army had entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang, Guanzhong was greatly shaken; Censor-in-Chief Buji and Libationer Ahudai were made concurrent Ministers of Agriculture, enrolled militia, supervised autumn taxes, and ordered the people into fortified settlements as a plan to avoid relocation.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that the main army had entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang, Guanzhong was thrown into panic; Buji and Ahudai were made concurrent agriculture ministers, enrolled militia, collected autumn taxes, and ordered people into fortified settlements against evacuation.

sentences.zh: 當時議者以謂大兵未至而河南先亂，且曰：「禦史監察城洛陽，治書供帳北使，中丞下兼司農簽軍督稅，台政可知矣。」

translations.literal: Commentators of the time said the great army had not yet arrived yet Henan was already in disorder, and also said: "Censors supervise the walls of Luoyang, judicial secretaries supply provisions for northern envoys, the censor-in-chief descends to concurrently hold agriculture and enroll troops and supervise taxes—the censorate's government can be known from this."
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Henan was in chaos before the main army even arrived and remarked: "Censors inspect Luoyang's walls, judicial secretaries entertain northern envoys, and the censor-in-chief enrolls militia and collects taxes as agriculture minister—one can see the state of the censorate."

sentences.zh: 至是，上謂撒合輦曰：「諺雲水深見長人。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor said to Sa Henian: "The proverb says, in deep water one sees tall men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told Sa Henian: "The proverb says that in deep water one sees who is truly tall.

sentences.zh: 朝臣或欲我一戰，汝獨言當靜以待之，與朕意合，今日有太平之望，皆汝謀也。

translations.literal: Some court ministers wished us to fight one battle; you alone said we should wait quietly—this matches my intent. Today's hope of peace is all your planning.
translations.idiomatic: Some ministers wanted a single decisive battle, but you alone urged patience, which matched my mind. Today's hope of peace is your doing.

sentences.zh: 先帝嘗言汝可用，可謂知人矣。」

translations.literal: The late emperor once said you could be employed—one may say he knew men."
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor said you were fit for service; he truly knew men."

sentences.zh: 未幾，右拾遺李大節、右司諫陳規言撒合輦諂佞納賄及不公事，奏帖留中不報。

translations.literal: Before long Right Reminder Li Dajie and Right Remonstrance Officer Chen Gui spoke of Sa Henian's flattery, sycophancy, taking bribes, and unfair conduct; the memorial was kept within and not reported.
translations.idiomatic: Soon remembrancer Li Dajie and remonstrance officer Chen Gui accused Henian of flattery, bribery, and injustice; the memorial was kept within and never answered.

sentences.zh: 明惠皇后嘗傳旨戒曰：「汝諂事上，上之騎鞠皆汝所教。」

translations.literal: Empress Minghui once transmitted an order of admonition saying: "You flatter and serve the sovereign; the sovereign's polo is all taught by you."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Minghui once sent word of warning: "You flatter the sovereign; even his polo is taught by you."

sentences.zh: 尉忻亦極言之，上頗悟，出為中京留守、兼行樞密院事。

translations.literal: Wei Xin also spoke to the extreme; the emperor came to understand somewhat and sent him out as Central Capital Defender and concurrent Touring Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xin spoke just as strongly; the emperor took the hint and posted Henian out as Central Capital defender with concurrent touring bureau of military affairs duties.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗改河南府為金昌府，號中京，又擬少室山頂為禦營，命移剌粘合築之，至是撒合輦為留守。

translations.literal: Earlier Emperor Xuanzong changed Henan Prefecture to Jinchang Prefecture, styled Central Capital, and also planned the summit of Mount Shaoshi as an imperial camp, ordering Yila Nihehe to build it; at this time Sa Henian was defender.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had renamed Henan Prefecture Jinchang Prefecture and styled it Central Capital, planned an imperial camp on Mount Shaoshi's summit, and ordered Yila Nihehe to build it; Henian was now posted as defender.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，北兵從河清徑渡，分兵至洛，出沒四十餘日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year northern troops crossed directly from Heqing, divided forces to reach Luo, and appeared and vanished for more than forty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 9 northern troops crossed at Heqing, sent detachments to Luoyang, and raided the vicinity for more than forty days.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥，立砲攻城。

translations.literal: On yihai of the second month they set up cannon to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai of the second month they erected siege cannon.

sentences.zh: 洛中初無軍，得三峰潰卒三四千人，與忠孝軍百餘守禦。

translations.literal: At first there were no troops in Luo; they obtained three or four thousand routed soldiers from Sanfeng and a hundred-odd Zhongxiao Army men to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang at first had no garrison; three or four thousand Sanfeng rout survivors and a little over a hundred Zhongxiao troops held the walls.

sentences.zh: 時輦疽發於背，不能軍，同知溫蒂罕斡朵羅主軍務，有大事則就輦稟之。

translations.literal: At the time Henian had an abscess on his back and could not command troops; Associate Administrator Wentihen Woduoluo handled military affairs, and on major matters he would go to Henian to report.
translations.idiomatic: Henian had a carbuncle on his back and could not take the field; associate administrator Wentihen Woduoluo ran military affairs and consulted Henian on major decisions.

sentences.zh: 三月甲申，忠孝軍百餘騎入使宅，強擁輦出奔，輦不得已從之，並以官屬及其子自隨，才出南裏城門，城上軍覺，閉之甕城中，矢石亂下，人馬多死傷。

translations.literal: On jiashen of the third month more than a hundred Zhongxiao Army horsemen entered the envoy's residence, forcibly escorted Henian out to flee; Henian had no choice but to follow, taking officials and his son with him; they had just exited the south inner city gate when troops on the wall noticed, closed them in the barbican, arrows and stones rained down, and many men and horses were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen of the third month more than a hundred Zhongxiao horsemen burst into the residence and forced Henian to flee with his staff and son; as they passed the south inner gate the wall garrison noticed, shut the barbican on them, and arrows and stones killed many men and horses.

sentences.zh: 輦知不能出，仰呼求救，軍士知出奔非輦意，以繩引而上，送入其宅，不敢出。

translations.literal: Henian knew he could not get out, looked up and called for rescue; the soldiers knew the flight was not Henian's intent, drew him up with ropes, sent him back into his residence, and he dared not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Henian, trapped, cried for help; the soldiers knew he had not meant to flee, hauled him back up by rope, and returned him to his residence, where he dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 鎮撫官縛出奔之黨，欲殺之，已斬三人，輦親為乞命，得免。

translations.literal: The pacification officer bound the party of fugitives and wished to kill them; three had already been beheaded when Henian personally begged for their lives and they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification officer seized the fugitives and had already beheaded three when Henian personally pleaded for their lives and saved the rest.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，斡朵羅齎金帛出北門，如前日巡城犒軍之狀，既出即沿城而西，直出外壕，城上人呼曰：「同知講和去矣。」

translations.literal: On yiyou Woduoluo carried gold and silks out the north gate as on the previous day when he had inspected the walls and rewarded the army; once out he followed the wall west, went straight outside the moat, and those on the wall called: "The associate administrator has gone to negotiate peace."
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Woduoluo carried gold and silk out the north gate as if to reward the troops on wall inspection, then followed the wall west and went straight out beyond the moat; men on the wall shouted: "The associate administrator has gone to sue for peace!"

sentences.zh: 軍士及將領隨而下者三四百人。

translations.literal: Soldiers and officers who followed down numbered three or four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Three or four hundred soldiers and officers followed him down.

sentences.zh: 少之，輦傳令雲：「同知叛降，有再下城者斬。」

translations.literal: Shortly after, Henian transmitted an order saying: "The associate administrator has rebelled and surrendered; whoever again descends the wall will be beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Henian issued an order: "The associate administrator has defected; anyone who leaves the wall again will be executed."

sentences.zh: 凡斬三四人，乃定。

translations.literal: In all three or four were beheaded, and then it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: After three or four executions the panic subsided.

sentences.zh: 丙戌夜，城東北角破，輦奪南門出不得，投濠水死。

translations.literal: On the night of bingxu the northeast corner of the wall was broken; Henian seized the south gate but could not get out and threw himself into the moat water and died.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of bingxu the northeast corner of the wall collapsed; Henian tried the south gate, could not escape, and drowned himself in the moat.

sentences.zh: 已而，大兵退，強伸複立帥府。

translations.literal: Before long the great army withdrew and Qiang Shen again established the command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army withdrew, Qiang Shen re-established the command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 強伸，本河中射糧軍子弟，貌極寢陋，而膂力過人。

translations.literal: Qiang Shen was originally a son of the grain-shooting army of Hedong; his appearance was extremely homely, yet his physical strength surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Shen came from the grain-shooting army of Hedong; he was homely in appearance but possessed extraordinary strength.

sentences.zh: 興定初，從華州副都統安寧複潼關，以勞任使，嘗監郃陽醋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingding he followed Hua Prefecture Deputy Metropolitan Commander An Ning to recover Tong Pass; for his merit he was given employment and once supervised Heyang vinegar.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingding era he followed Hua deputy commander An Ning in retaking Tong Pass, was rewarded with appointment, and once supervised the Heyang vinegar monopoly.

sentences.zh: 後客洛下，選充官軍，戍陝鐵嶺，軍潰被虜，從都尉兀林答胡土竄歸中京。

translations.literal: Later he sojourned below Luo, was selected to fill the official army, garrisoned Shaan at Tieling, the army was routed and he was captured; he fled back to Central Capital with Commandant Wulindahutu.
translations.idiomatic: He later went to Luoyang, was enrolled in the regular army, garrisoned Tieling in Shaan, was captured when the army collapsed, and fled back to Central Capital with commandant Wulindahutu.

sentences.zh: 時中京已破，留守兼行樞密院使內族撒合輦死之，元帥任守真複立府事，以便宜署伸警巡使。

translations.literal: At that time Central Capital had already been broken; Defender and concurrent Touring Bureau of Military Affairs imperial clansman Sa Henian died in it; Marshal Ren Shouzhen again established headquarters affairs and by discretionary authority appointed Shen patrol commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Central Capital had already fallen; defender Sa Henian had died; marshal Ren Shouzhen re-established headquarters and appointed Shen patrol commissioner on discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 後守真率部曲軍從行省思烈入援，鄭州之敗，守真死。

translations.literal: Later Shouzhen led his personal troops following Branch Secretariat Silie to enter as relief; at the defeat at Zheng Prefecture Shouzhen died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shouzhen led his household troops with branch secretariat Silie to relieve Zheng Prefecture and died in the defeat there.

sentences.zh: 天興元年八月，中京人推伸為府簽事，領所有軍二千五百人，傷殘老幼半之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianxing the people of Central Capital pushed Shen as prefectural signing officer, leading all troops of twenty-five hundred, of whom wounded, crippled, old, and young were half.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianxing 1 the people of Central Capital chose Shen as prefectural signing officer with twenty-five hundred troops, half of them wounded, aged, or boys.

sentences.zh: 甫三日，北兵圍之，東西北三面多樹大砲。

translations.literal: Only three days later northern troops besieged it; on the east, north, and west sides they set up many large cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days northern troops besieged the city and erected heavy cannon on the east, north, and west.

sentences.zh: 伸括衣帛為幟，立之城上，率士卒赤身而戰，以壯士五十人往來救應，大叫，以「憨子軍」為號，其聲勢與萬眾無異。

translations.literal: Shen gathered clothing and silks for banners and set them on the walls; he led soldiers to fight stripped to the waist, with fifty stalwarts going back and forth in rescue and response, shouting loudly, using "Simpleton Army" as their cry—their sound and force were no different from ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shen hung banners of cloth and silk on the walls, led his men to fight stripped to the waist, and sent fifty stalwarts to rush wherever needed, shouting the battle cry "Simpleton Army" until their roar sounded like ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 兵器已盡，以錢為鏃，得大兵一箭，截而為四，以筒鞭發之。

translations.literal: Weapons were exhausted; they used coins for arrowheads; obtaining one northern arrow they cut it into four and launched them with tube whips.
translations.idiomatic: When weapons ran out they used coins for arrowheads; each enemy arrow they captured was cut into four and shot back with tube slings.

sentences.zh: 又創遏砲，用不過數人，能發大石于百步外，所擊無不中。

translations.literal: He also devised a blocking cannon needing no more than several men, able to launch great stones beyond a hundred paces; what it struck never missed.
translations.idiomatic: He also devised a blocking catapult manned by only a few men that could hurl boulders more than a hundred paces with unerring aim.

sentences.zh: 伸奔走四應，所至必捷。

translations.literal: Shen ran about responding on all four sides; wherever he arrived there was sure success.
translations.idiomatic: Shen raced to every threatened point and always prevailed.

sentences.zh: 得二駝及所乘馬皆殺之，以犒軍士，人不過一啖，而得者如百金之賜。

translations.literal: Obtaining two camels and the horse he rode, he killed them all to reward the soldiers; each man received no more than one bite, yet those who got it were like receiving a gift of a hundred in gold.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered two camels and his own mount to feed the troops; each man received barely a mouthful, yet a share was prized like a hundred pieces of gold.

sentences.zh: 九月，大兵退百里外。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the great army withdrew a hundred li away.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the main army withdrew a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 閏月，複攻，兵數倍於前。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month they attacked again with troops several times those before.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month they attacked again with several times the former force.

sentences.zh: 又一月，不能拔。

translations.literal: Another month passed and they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Another month passed and they still could not take the city.

sentences.zh: 事聞，哀宗降詔褒諭，以伸為中京留守、元帥左都監、世襲謀克、行元帥府事。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Emperor Aizong issued an edict of praise and commendation, appointing Shen Central Capital Defender, Marshal Left Metropolitan Supervisor, hereditary company commander, and exercising marshalate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Emperor Aizong praised him and appointed him Central Capital defender, marshal left metropolitan supervisor, hereditary company commander, with authority over the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 十月，參知政事內族思烈自南山領軍民十余萬入洛，行省事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Participating Administrator imperial clansman Silie from the southern mountains led more than a hundred thousand soldiers and civilians into Luo and conducted branch secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month participating administrator Silie led more than a hundred thousand soldiers and civilians from the southern hills into Luoyang and took charge of branch secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，伸建一堂於洛川驛之東，名曰「報恩」，刻詔文於石，願以死自效。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year Shen built a hall east of Luochuan Post Station called "Repaying Grace," carved the edict text on stone, and vowed to offer his death in service.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2 Shen built a hall east of Luochuan post station called Repaying Grace, carved the imperial edict in stone, and vowed to die in the state's service.

sentences.zh: 三月，中使至，以伸便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third month an imperial envoy arrived and granted Shen discretionary authority to act as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an imperial envoy arrived and authorized Shen to act at his discretion.

sentences.zh: 是月，大兵自汴驅思烈之子於東門下，誘思烈降。

translations.literal: That month the great army from Bian drove Silie's son below the east gate to entice Silie to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That month the main army from Bian drove Silie's son before the east gate to tempt Silie into surrender.

sentences.zh: 思烈即命左右射之，既而知崔立之變，病不能語而死。

translations.literal: Silie at once ordered those beside him to shoot him; afterward learning of Cui Li's mutiny, he fell ill, could not speak, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Silie immediately ordered his attendants to shoot the boy; when he learned of Cui Li's coup he fell ill, lost speech, and died.

sentences.zh: 總帥忽林答胡土代行省事，伸行總帥府事，月餘糧盡，軍民稍稍散去。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Hulindahutu acted in branch secretariat affairs; Shen conducted commander-in-chief headquarters affairs; after more than a month grain was exhausted and soldiers and civilians gradually scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Hulindahutu took over branch secretariat affairs while Shen ran the commander headquarters; after a month supplies ran out and troops and civilians drifted away.

sentences.zh: 五月，大兵複來，陣于洛南，伸陣水北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the great army came again, forming battle lines south of Luo; Shen formed lines north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the main army returned, drawing up south of Luoyang while Shen formed his line north of the river.

sentences.zh: 有韓帥者匹馬立水濱，招伸降，伸謂帥曰：「君獨非我家臣子耶？

translations.literal: A Commander Han stood alone on horseback by the water's edge and summoned Shen to surrender; Shen said to Han: "Are you not alone a servant and son of our house?
translations.idiomatic: A commander Han stood alone on the riverbank and called on Shen to surrender; Shen said: "Are you not a servant of our house?

sentences.zh: 一日勤王，猶遺令名於世，君既不能，乃欲誘我降耶？

translations.literal: For one day serving the throne in peril still leaves a fine name in the world; since you cannot do even that, do you now wish to entice me to surrender?
translations.idiomatic: Even a single day of loyal service leaves a name for the ages; since you could not manage that, do you now mean to tempt me to surrender?

sentences.zh: 我本一軍卒，今貴為留守，誓以死報國耳。」

translations.literal: I was originally but a common soldier; now I am honored as defender—I swear only to repay the state with death."
translations.idiomatic: I was only a common soldier; now I am defender of the city, and I swear to die for the state."

sentences.zh: 遂躍而射之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he leaped forward and shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: He leaped forward and shot at him.

sentences.zh: 帥奔陣，率步卒數百奪橋，伸軍一旗手獨出拒之，殺數人，伸乃手解都統銀符與之佩，士卒氣複振。

translations.literal: Han ran back to his formation, led several hundred infantry to seize the bridge; one bannerman of Shen's army alone came out to resist, killed several men, and Shen personally unfastened the metropolitan supervisor's silver tally and gave it for him to wear—the soldiers' spirit revived.
translations.idiomatic: Han fled to his line and led several hundred foot soldiers to seize the bridge; one of Shen's standard-bearers charged out alone, killed several men, and Shen personally gave him the metropolitan supervisor's silver tally; the troops' morale revived.

sentences.zh: 初，築戰壘於城外四隅，至五門內外皆有屏，謂之迷魂牆。

translations.literal: Earlier he had built battle ramparts at the four corners outside the city; within and without the five gates there were screens all called Soul-Bewildering Walls.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier built fighting ramparts at the four outer corners and screening walls inside and outside the five gates, called Soul-Bewildering Walls.

sentences.zh: 大兵以五百騎迫之，伸率卒二百鼓噪而出，大兵退。

translations.literal: The great army pressed with five hundred cavalry; Shen led two hundred troops shouting and drumming out, and the great army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The main army pressed with five hundred horsemen; Shen led two hundred men out with shouts and drums, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六月，行省胡土率眾走南山，鷹揚都尉獻西門以降，伸知城不能守，率死士數十人突東門出，轉戰至偃師，力盡就執。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Branch Secretariat Hutu led the masses to flee to the southern mountains; Yingyang Commandant presented the west gate to surrender; Shen knew the city could not be held, led several tens of death-dedicated warriors to burst out the east gate, fought in turn as far as Yanshi, strength exhausted and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month branch secretariat Hutu fled south with his force; Yingyang commandant opened the west gate in surrender; Shen, knowing the city was lost, broke out the east gate with several dozen devoted men, fought his way to Yanshi, and was captured when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 載以一馬，擁迫而行。

translations.literal: He was loaded on one horse and forced along under pressure.
translations.idiomatic: They put him on a horse and hustled him along.

sentences.zh: 伸宛轉不肯進，強掖之，將見大帥塔察。

translations.literal: Shen twisted and would not advance; they forcibly supported him, intending to present him to Grand Marshal Tacha.
translations.idiomatic: Shen twisted and refused to go forward; they dragged him along to present him to grand marshal Tacha.

sentences.zh: 及中京七里河，伸語不遜，兵卒相謂曰：「此人乖角如此，若見大帥，其能降乎？

translations.literal: When they reached Qili River of Central Capital, Shen's words were insubordinate; the soldiers said to one another: "This man's perversity is such—if he sees the grand marshal, how can he surrender?
translations.idiomatic: At Qili River near Central Capital Shen spoke defiantly; the soldiers said to one another: "This man is so stubborn—if he sees the grand marshal, will he ever submit?

sentences.zh: 不若殺之。」
