translations.literal: Better to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Better kill him now."

sentences.zh: 因好語誘之曰：「汝能北面一屈膝，吾貸汝命。」

translations.literal: They therefore used kind words to entice him: "If you can face north and bend one knee, I will spare your life."
translations.idiomatic: They coaxed him: "Face north and bow once and we will spare your life."

sentences.zh: 伸不從，左右力持使北面，伸拗頭南向，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Shen would not obey; those beside him forcibly held him to face north; Shen twisted his head to face south, and they thereupon killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen refused; his guards forced him to turn north, but he wrenched his head southward, and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 烏林答胡土

translations.literal: Wulindahutu
translations.idiomatic: Wulindahutu

sentences.zh: 烏林答胡土。

translations.literal: Wulindahutu.
translations.idiomatic: Wulindahutu.

sentences.zh: 正大九年正月戊子，北兵以河中一軍由洛陽東四十里白坡渡河。

translations.literal: On wuzi of the first month of the ninth year of Zhengda northern troops with one Hezhong army crossed the river at Baipo, forty li east of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi of the first month of Zhengda 9 a Hezhong army crossed the river at Baipo, forty li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 白坡故河清縣，河有石底，歲旱水不能尋丈。

translations.literal: Baipo was the former site of Heqing County; the river has a stone bottom, and in years of drought the water cannot reach a full zhang in depth.
translations.idiomatic: Baipo had been Heqing County; with its rocky riverbed, even in drought the water seldom rose to eight feet.

sentences.zh: 國初以三千騎由此路趨汴，是後縣廢為鎮，宣宗南遷，河防上下千里，常以此路為憂，每冬日命洛陽一軍戍之。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state three thousand horsemen by this route hastened toward Bian; afterward the county was abolished and made a town; when the Xuanzong moved south, along the thousand-li river defenses this route was always a worry, and every winter day a Luoyang army was ordered to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding three thousand horsemen had taken this road to Bian; later the county was reduced to a town. After the Xuanzong moved south, the thousand-li river line was always troubled by this crossing, and each winter a Luoyang garrison was posted there.

sentences.zh: 河中破，有言此路可徒涉者，已而果然。

translations.literal: When Hezhong fell, someone said this route could be waded on foot; before long it proved so.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhong fell someone said the ford could be crossed on foot, and before long it was.

sentences.zh: 北兵既渡，奪河陰官舟以濟諸軍。

translations.literal: Once the northern troops had crossed, they seized Heyin government boats to ferry the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Once across, the northern troops seized government boats at Heyin to ferry the rest of the army.

sentences.zh: 時胡土為破虜都尉，戍潼關，以去冬十二月被旨入援，至偃師，聞白坡徑渡之耗，直趨少室，夜至少林寺。

translations.literal: At the time Hutu was Defender Who Breaks the Barbarians, garrisoning Tong Pass; in the twelfth month of last winter he received orders to enter in relief, reached Yanshi, heard word of the Baipo direct crossing, went straight to Shaoshi, and by night reached Shaolin Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu was then Defender Who Breaks the Barbarians, stationed at Tong Pass. Ordered south the previous twelfth month, he reached Yanshi, heard of the crossing at Baipo, turned straight for Shaoshi, and reached Shaolin Temple that night.

sentences.zh: 時登封縣官民已遷太平頂禦寨。

translations.literal: By then the officials and people of Dengfeng County had already moved to the Taiping Peak defense stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Dengfeng had already withdrawn to the stockade on Taiping Peak.

sentences.zh: 明日，胡土使人紿縣官雲：「吾軍中家屬輜重欲留此山，即率兵赴汴京。」

translations.literal: Next day Hutu sent men to deceive the county magistrate, saying: "My army's families and baggage wish to remain on this mountain; I shall presently lead troops to Bianjing."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hutu sent men to deceive the county magistrate: "My dependents and baggage will stay on this mountain while I lead the army to Bian."

sentences.zh: 因攝縣官下山，使之前導，一軍隨之而上。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took charge of the county magistrate down the mountain, made him go ahead as guide, and one army followed him up.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the magistrate down the mountain as his guide while a detachment followed up behind.

sentences.zh: 山既險固，糧亦充足，遂有久住之意。

translations.literal: The mountain being steep and secure and grain also ample, he then had a mind to stay long.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain was steep and well supplied, and he began to think of staying.

sentences.zh: 尋縱軍下山劫掠居民，甚于盜賊，旁近一二百里無不被害。

translations.literal: Soon he let the army down the mountain to plunder the people, worse than bandits; for a hundred or two hundred li round none escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he let his men down to plunder the countryside worse than bandits; for a hundred or two hundred li around none escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 胡土畏變，知而不禁，又所劫牛畜糧糗，亦分有之。

translations.literal: Hutu feared mutiny, knew yet did not forbid it, and also took a share of the cattle, grain, and provisions plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu feared mutiny, knew what was happening yet did not stop it, and took his own share of the cattle, grain, and fodder seized.

sentences.zh: 七月，恆山公武仙、參政思烈兩行省軍，屯登封城南大林下，遣人約之入京。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Prince Hengshan Wu Xian and Participating Administrator Silie's two branch secretariat armies encamped below the great forest south of Dengfeng city and sent men to summon him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the two branch secretariat armies of Prince Hengshan Wu Xian and participating administrator Silie camped in the great woods south of Dengfeng and sent to summon him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 胡土百計不肯下，不得已，乃分其軍四千，與思烈俱東。

translations.literal: Hutu by every scheme refused to come down; having no choice, he then divided four thousand of his troops and went east with Silie.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu used every excuse to stay on the mountain; only under compulsion did he detach four thousand men and march east with Silie.

sentences.zh: 八月三日，兩行省軍潰于中牟，胡土狼狽上山，殘卒三二十人外偏裨無一人至者。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eighth month the two branch secretariat armies were routed at Zhongmou; Hutu in disarray fled up the mountain, and beyond thirty-odd survivors not one deputy or staff officer arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of the eighth month both armies were routed at Zhongmou. Hutu fled in disorder up the mountain with only thirty-odd survivors; not a single officer rejoined him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，思烈自留山行省於中京，徵兵同保洛陽，又遷延不行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Silie from his mountain branch secretariat at Central Capital gathered troops jointly to hold Luoyang, yet again delayed and would not march.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Silie, who had kept his branch secretariat on the mountain at Central Capital, called up troops to hold Luoyang jointly, yet again delayed and would not march.

sentences.zh: 思烈以檄來，言：「若依前逗留，自有典憲，吾不汝容矣。」

translations.literal: Silie sent a proclamation saying: "If as before you linger, there are statutes for that—I shall not spare you."
translations.idiomatic: Silie sent a written order: "If you linger as before, the statutes apply, and I will not spare you."

sentences.zh: 胡土懼，乃挈妻子及軍往中京，留其半山上以為巢穴。

translations.literal: Hutu was afraid and took wife, children, and army to Central Capital, leaving half on the mountain as a nest.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Hutu took his wife, children, and troops to Central Capital, leaving half his force on the mountain as a refuge.

sentences.zh: 天興二年三月，思烈病卒，留語胡土代行省事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Tianxing Silie died of illness and left word for Hutu to act in branch secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianxing 2 Silie died of illness and left instructions for Hutu to take over branch secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 六月，敵勢益重，強伸方盡力戰禦，而胡土即領輕騎、挈妻子棄城南奔，遂失中京。

translations.literal: In the sixth month enemy pressure grew heavier; Qiang Shen was fighting hard in defense, but Hutu at once led light cavalry and took wife and children abandoning the south of the city to flee, and Central Capital was lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the enemy pressed harder. Qiang Shen was fighting with all his strength, but Hutu at once led light cavalry away with his wife and children, abandoned the south of the city, and fled, and Central Capital was lost.

sentences.zh: 初，胡土在太平頂既顧望不進，又懼人議己，乃出榜募人為救駕軍，雲：「一旅之眾可以興複國家，諸人有能奮發許國捐軀者，豈不濟大事乎！」

translations.literal: Earlier, on Taiping Peak Hutu had both looked back and not advanced and feared men would speak of him; he therefore posted a notice to recruit men for an army to rescue the throne, saying: "One company can restore the state—if any among you can rouse himself to serve the realm and give body and life, will that not accomplish the great affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on Taiping Peak Hutu had hung back and feared criticism, so he posted a notice recruiting a rescue-the-throne army: "A single company can restore the state. If any of you will rouse yourselves to serve the realm and give your lives, will that not finish the great task?"

sentences.zh: 於是，不逞之徒隨募而出，得澤人緝麻觜、武錄事等二十餘人，促令赴京。

translations.literal: Thereupon discontented fellows followed the recruitment and came forth—he got more than twenty such as Ze's Jima Zui and military recorder, and urged them to go to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Discontented men answered the call. He gathered more than twenty, including Jima Zui of Ze and a military recorder, and hurried them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 行及盧店，即行劫，械至，杖之二百，人無不竊笑。

translations.literal: When they reached Ludian they at once robbed on the road; brought to punishment, he caned them two hundred strokes, and none failed to snicker in secret.
translations.idiomatic: At Ludian they began robbing on the road. Brought before him, they were flogged two hundred strokes, and everyone secretly laughed.

sentences.zh: 既而走蔡州，上召見慰問，而心薄之。

translations.literal: Presently they went to Cai Prefecture; the emperor summoned and consoled them, yet in heart held them cheap.
translations.idiomatic: They then went to Cai Prefecture. The emperor summoned and consoled them, but inwardly thought little of them.

sentences.zh: 會宋人攻唐州，元帥烏古論黑漢屢遣人告急，即命胡土領忠孝軍百人，就征西山招撫烏古論換住、黃八兒等軍赴之。

translations.literal: When Song men attacked Tangzhou, Marshal Wugulun Heihan repeatedly sent men in urgent plea; he at once ordered Hutu to lead a hundred Loyal and Filial Army troops to proceed on campaign to the Western Hills to summon and pacify Wugulun Huanzhu, Huang Ba'er, and other armies to go there.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song attacked Tangzhou, Marshal Wugulun Heihan sent repeated urgent appeals. Hutu was ordered to lead a hundred Loyal and Filial troops west to summon Wugulun Huanzhu, Huang Ba'er, and other forces to the relief.

sentences.zh: 胡土率兵至唐，宋人斂避，縱其半入城，夾擊之，胡土大敗，僅存三十騎以還，換住死焉。

translations.literal: Hutu led troops to Tang; Song men drew back in avoidance, let half his force enter the city, and struck from both sides; Hutu was greatly defeated, barely thirty horsemen returning; Huanzhu died there.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu marched to Tang. The Song drew back, let half his force into the city, then struck from both sides. Hutu was routed and returned with only thirty horsemen; Huanzhu was killed.

sentences.zh: 既而以胡土為殿前都點檢，罷權參政。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hutu was made Palace Front Chief Inspector and dismissed from acting participating administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Hutu was then made Palace Front chief inspector and removed from acting participating administrator.

sentences.zh: 大兵圍蔡，分軍防守，胡土守西面。

translations.literal: The main army besieged Cai; forces were divided for defense, and Hutu defended the west face.
translations.idiomatic: The main army besieged Cai. Forces were divided for defense, and Hutu held the west wall.

sentences.zh: 十一月，胡土之奴竊其金牌，夜縋城降，朝士喧播謂胡土縱之往，將有異志。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Hutu's slave stole his gold tally, by night let himself down the wall to surrender; courtiers spread word that Hutu had let him go and would have other intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Hutu's slave stole his gold tally and let himself down the wall at night to surrender. Courtiers spread word that Hutu had let him go and harbored other designs.

sentences.zh: 胡土聞之，內不自安，乞解軍職。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Hutu was inwardly ill at ease and begged to be relieved of military office.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Hutu grew uneasy and asked to be relieved of his military post.

sentences.zh: 上慰之曰：「卿父子昆弟皆為帥臣，受恩不為不厚，顧肯降耶。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled him saying: "You father, sons, and brothers are all commanders; favor received is not thin—would you really be willing to surrender?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consoled him: "Your father, sons, and brothers have all been commanders. The favor shown you is not slight. Would you really surrender?

sentences.zh: 且卿向在洛陽不即降，而千里遠來降於蔡，豈人情也哉。

translations.literal: And before, when you were at Luoyang you did not at once surrender, yet came a thousand li to surrender at Cai—is that human feeling?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, you did not surrender at once when you were at Luoyang, yet you came a thousand li to surrender at Cai. Does that sound like human nature?

sentences.zh: 聞卿遇奴太察，且其衣食不常給之，此蓋往求溫飽耳，卿何慊焉。」

translations.literal: I hear you treat the slave too strictly and do not regularly supply his clothing and food—he surely went seeking warmth and plenty; why be bitter over it?"
translations.idiomatic: I hear you are too harsh with the slave and do not regularly provide his food and clothing. He surely went seeking comfort. Why be bitter about it?"

sentences.zh: 因賜饌以安其心。

translations.literal: He therefore gave delicacies to settle his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him a feast to set his mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 初，胡土罷機政，頗有怨言，左右勸上誅之，上不聽。

translations.literal: Earlier when Hutu was dismissed from machine government he had many complaints; attendants urged the emperor to put him to death, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hutu was removed from government affairs he had complained bitterly. Attendants urged the emperor to execute him, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及令守西城，尤怏怏不樂，至是始感恩無他慮矣。

translations.literal: When ordered to defend the west city he was especially sullen and unhappy; only then did he begin to feel grateful and have no other thought.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to hold the west wall he was especially resentful. Only now did he feel grateful and lay aside other thoughts.

sentences.zh: 尋以總帥孛術魯婁室與胡土皆權參政，婁室與右丞仲德同事，胡土防守如故，複以都尉承麟為東面元帥權總帥。

translations.literal: Soon Commander-in-Chief Shulutu Loushi and Hutu were both acting participating administrators; Loushi with Right Chancellor Zhongde handled affairs together; Hutu defended as before; again Defender-in-Chief Chenglins was made eastern face marshal with acting overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon commander-in-chief Shulutu Loushi and Hutu were both made acting participating administrators. Loushi worked with right chancellor Zhongde while Hutu continued his defense. Defender Chenglins was again made eastern marshal with acting overall command.

sentences.zh: 先是，攻東城，婁室隨機備禦。

translations.literal: Earlier when they attacked the east city, Loushi guarded as occasion demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the east wall was attacked, Loushi had defended as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 二日移攻南城，烏古論鎬易之，砲擊城樓幾僕，右丞仲德率軍救援，乃罷攻。

translations.literal: On the second day they shifted attack to the south city; Wugulun Hao replaced him; catapults nearly toppled the tower; Right Chancellor Zhongde led troops to rescue and only then stopped the attack.
translations.idiomatic: On the second day the attack shifted to the south wall and Wugulun Hao took over. Catapults nearly brought down the tower. Right chancellor Zhongde led a relief force and the assault was called off.

sentences.zh: 俄而四面受敵，仲德艱於獨援，遂薦承麟代婁室東面，而乞與婁室同救應。

translations.literal: Before long on four sides they bore attack; Zhongde was hard pressed alone to aid, and recommended Chenglins to replace Loushi on the east while begging to rescue together with Loushi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the city was attacked on four sides. Zhongde could not sustain relief alone and recommended Chenglins to replace Loushi on the east while asking to assist Loushi jointly.

sentences.zh: 初，胡土失外城，頗慚恨，聲言力小不能令眾，仲德亦薦之，故有是命。

translations.literal: Earlier when Hutu lost the outer city he was quite ashamed and resentful, declaring his strength was small and he could not command the masses; Zhongde also recommended him, hence this order.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hutu lost the outer city he was ashamed and claimed his force was too small to command the troops. Zhongde also recommended him, hence this appointment.

sentences.zh: 蔡城破，投汝水死。

translations.literal: When Cai city fell, he threw himself into the Ru River and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai fell he threw himself into the Ru River and died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：撒合輦本以佞進，烏林答胡土戰陣不武，付以孤城，望其捍禦大難，豈得為知人乎。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Sa Henian rose by flattery; Wulindahutu was not martial in battle—entrusting him with an isolated city and expecting him to ward off great peril, can that be called knowing men?
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Sa Henian advanced through flattery; Wulindahutu was no warrior in battle. To entrust an isolated city to him and expect him to ward off catastrophe—can that be called knowing men?

sentences.zh: 強伸一射糧卒耳，及授以兵，乃能應變制勝，遠過二人，力盡乃斃，猶有烈丈夫之風焉。

translations.literal: Qiang Shen was but a grain-quota archer; once given troops he could adapt and overcome—far surpassing the two; strength spent he died, yet still had the bearing of a fierce gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Shen was only a grain-quota archer, yet once given troops he could adapt and win, far surpassing the other two. He died only when his strength was spent, and still showed the spirit of a true man.

sentences.zh: 古人有言：「四郊多壘，拔士為將。」

translations.literal: The ancients said: "When the four suburbs are full of enemy camps, raise men from the ranks to be generals."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "When the suburbs on four sides are full of enemy camps, promote men from the ranks to be generals."

sentences.zh: 使金運未去，伸足以建功名矣夫。

translations.literal: Had Jin's fortune not yet departed, Shen would have been enough to establish fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Had Jin's fortune not waned, Shen would have been enough to win lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 完顏思烈

translations.literal: Wanyan Silie
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Silie

sentences.zh: 內族思烈，南陽郡王襄之子也。

translations.literal: Of the inner clan, Silie was son of Prince Nanyang Wang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Silie of the inner clan was the son of Prince of Nanyang, Wang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 資性詳雅，頗知書史。

translations.literal: By nature composed and refined, he knew somewhat of books and history.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was composed and refined and knew something of books and history.

sentences.zh: 自五六歲入宮充奉禦，甚見寵倖，世號曰「自在奉禦」。

translations.literal: From five or six he entered the palace as attendant, greatly favored; the world called him "Self-Possessed Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: From the age of five or six he entered the palace as an attendant and was greatly favored. People called him the "Self-Possessed Attendant."

sentences.zh: 當宣宗入承大統，胡沙虎跋扈，思烈尚在髫齔，嘗涕泣跪抱帝膝致說曰：「願早誅權臣，以靖王室。」

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong succeeded to the great succession and Hu Shahu was overbearing, Silie was still in childhood; he once wept kneeling and embracing the emperor's knee to plead: "I wish early to execute the powerful minister to settle the royal house."
translations.idiomatic: When the Xuanzong succeeded to the throne and Hu Shahu was overbearing, Silie was still a child. He once knelt weeping, embraced the emperor's knee, and said: "I beg that the powerful minister be executed early to settle the royal house."

sentences.zh: 帝急顧左右掩其口。

translations.literal: The emperor hurriedly looked to attendants to cover his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hurriedly signaled his attendants to cover the boy's mouth.

sentences.zh: 自是帝甚器重之。

translations.literal: From this the emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 後由提點近侍局遷都點檢。

translations.literal: Later from Supervisor of the Personal Attendance Bureau he was promoted Metropolitan Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted from supervisor of the Personal Attendance Bureau to metropolitan inspector.

sentences.zh: 天興元年，汴京被圍，哀宗以思烈權參知政事，行省事于鄧州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxing Bianjing was besieged; the Aizong made Silie acting participating administrator directing branch secretariat affairs at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxing Bian was besieged. The Aizong made Silie acting participating administrator and sent him to direct branch secretariat affairs at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 會武仙引兵入援，於是思烈率諸軍發自汝州，過密縣，遇大元兵，不用武仙阻澗之策，遂敗績于京水，語在《武仙傳》。

translations.literal: When Wu Xian led troops in relief, Silie then led the armies from Ruzhou; passing Mixian they met Great Yuan troops; not using Wu Xian's strategy to block at the ravine, he was defeated at Jingshui—as told in the Wu Xian biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Xian marched in relief, Silie led the armies from Ruzhou. Passing Mixian they met Great Yuan troops. Ignoring Wu Xian's plan to block them at the ravine, he was defeated at Jingshui, as told in Wu Xian's biography.

sentences.zh: 中京留守、元帥左監軍任守真死之。

translations.literal: Central Capital defender and marshal left supervising army Ren Shouzhen died in it.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Shouzhen, defender of Central Capital and left supervising marshal, died in the battle.

sentences.zh: 上聞，罷思烈行省之職，以守中京。

translations.literal: On report the emperor dismissed Silie's branch post and ordered him to hold Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor removed Silie's branch secretariat post and ordered him to hold Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 無何，大兵圍中京未能下，崔立遣人監思烈子於中京城下，招之使降。

translations.literal: Before long the main army besieged Central Capital without taking it; Cui Li sent men to supervise Silie's son below Central Capital's walls to summon him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the main army besieged Central Capital without taking it. Cui Li sent men to place Silie's son below the walls and summon him to surrender.

sentences.zh: 思烈不顧，令軍士射之。

translations.literal: Silie paid no heed and ordered soldiers to shoot.
translations.idiomatic: Silie paid no heed and ordered his soldiers to shoot.

sentences.zh: 既而知崔立已以汴京歸順，病數日而死。

translations.literal: After learning Cui Li had already surrendered Bianjing with allegiance, he fell ill several days and died.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Cui Li had already surrendered Bian, he fell ill and died within days.

sentences.zh: 初，思烈會武仙等軍入援，即與仙論議不同，仙以思烈方得君，每假借之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Silie joined Wu Xian and other armies in relief he differed in counsel with Xian; Xian because Silie had just won the ruler's trust always indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Silie joined Wu Xian and other relief armies, he and Wu Xian disagreed at once. Because Silie had just won the ruler's favor, Wu Xian always indulged him.

sentences.zh: 思烈謂仙本無入援意，特以朝廷遣一參政召兵，迫於不得已乃行耳。

translations.literal: Silie said Xian originally had no mind to enter relief but that the court sent one participating administrator to summon troops and he marched only under compulsion.
translations.idiomatic: Silie said Wu Xian had never meant to march in relief but had come only because the court sent a participating administrator to summon troops and he was forced to go.

sentences.zh: 然仙知兵，頗以持重為事。

translations.literal: Yet Xian knew warfare and quite made weight his principle.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wu Xian knew warfare and made caution his principle.

sentences.zh: 思烈急於入京，不聽仙策，於是左右司員外郎王渥乃勸思烈曰：「武仙大小數百戰，經涉不為不多，兵事當共議。」

translations.literal: Silie was urgent to enter the capital and would not hear Xian's plan; thereupon Left and Right Secretariat Outer Gentleman Wang Wo then urged Silie: "Wu Xian has fought hundreds of battles large and small, experience is not small—military affairs should be discussed together."
translations.idiomatic: Silie was eager to reach the capital and would not hear Wu Xian's advice. Thereupon Wang Wo, outer gentleman of the Left and Right Secretariat, urged Silie: "Wu Xian has fought hundreds of battles large and small. His experience is not slight. Military affairs should be discussed together."

sentences.zh: 思烈疑其與仙有謀，幾斬之，渥自以無愧於內，不懼也。

translations.literal: Silie suspected collusion with Xian and nearly beheaded him; Wo took himself as without fault inwardly and was not afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Silie suspected collusion with Wu Xian and nearly had him executed. Wo felt himself blameless inwardly and was not afraid.

sentences.zh: 已而思烈果敗，渥歿於陣。

translations.literal: Before long Silie was indeed defeated; Wo perished in the battle array.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Silie was indeed defeated, and Wo died in battle.

sentences.zh: 渥字仲澤，後名仲澤，太原人。

translations.literal: Wo styled Zhongze, later named Zhongze, a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wo, styled Zhongze and later also named Zhongze, was a man of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 性明俊不羈，博學善談論，工尺牘，字畫清美，有晉人風。

translations.literal: Bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled at discussion, adept at documents, writing clear and beautiful with Jin-ren style.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright and sharp, unrestrained by convention, broadly learned and skilled in discussion, adept at documents, and wrote with a clear, beautiful hand in the manner of the Jin period.

sentences.zh: 少遊太學，長於詞賦，登興定二年進士第。

translations.literal: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, excelled at lyrics and rhapsodies, passed the jinshi in the second year of Xingding.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, excelled at lyrics and rhapsodies, and passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xingding.

sentences.zh: 為時帥奧屯邦獻、完顏斜烈所知，故多在兵間。

translations.literal: Military commissioners Aotun Bangxian and Wanyan Xielie knew him, so he was often amid armies.
translations.idiomatic: The military commissioners Aotun Bangxian and Wanyan Xielie knew him, so he was often with the armies.

sentences.zh: 後辟寧陵令，有治跡，入為尚書省令史。

translations.literal: Later summoned as Magistrate of Ningling with governing traces, he entered as Secretariat clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He was later summoned as magistrate of Ningling, where he left traces of good governance, and then entered service as a clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 因使宋至揚州，應對敏給，宋人重之。

translations.literal: On mission to Song he reached Yangzhou, replied sharply, and Song men esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Song he reached Yangzhou, replied sharply, and the Song esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 及還，為太學助教，轉樞密院經歷官，俄遷右司都事，稍見信用。

translations.literal: On return he was Imperial Academy assistant instructor, transferred to Privy Council experiences officer, soon promoted Right Secretariat chief clerk, gradually gaining trust.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became an assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy, then transferred to an experience officer at the Privy Council, and soon rose to chief clerk of the Right Secretariat, gradually gaining trust.

sentences.zh: 及思烈往鄧州，以渥為左右司員外郎，從行。

translations.literal: When Silie went to Dengzhou, Wo was made Left and Right Secretariat outer gentleman and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Silie went to Dengzhou, Wo was made outer gentleman of the Left and Right Secretariat and accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：思烈夙惠，請誅權奸以立主威，有甘羅、辟疆之風，所謂「茂良不必父祖」者也。

translations.literal: Commentary: Silie from childhood showed talent, asked to kill powerful traitors to establish sovereign authority—has Gan Luo and Pi Jiang's wind; so-called "the excellent need not follow father and grandfather."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: Silie showed talent early, asking to kill powerful traitors to establish the sovereign's authority, with something of Gan Luo and Pi Jiang about him—what is meant by "the excellent need not follow father and grandfather."

sentences.zh: 中京之圍，崔立脅其子使招之降，不顧而趣射之，何愧乎橋玄。

translations.literal: At the siege of Central Capital Cui Li coerced his son to summon surrender; he paid no heed and urged shooting—what shame compared to Qiao Xuan?
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Central Capital, Cui Li coerced his son to summon him to surrender. Silie paid no heed and ordered his men to shoot. What shame is there compared with Qiao Xuan?

sentences.zh: 至如不從武仙之言，以至於敗，此蓋時人因惜王仲澤之死而有是言，仙無入援之意則非誣也。

translations.literal: As for not following Wu Xian's words leading to defeat—that is because contemporaries regretted Wang Zhongze's death and spoke thus; that Xian had no intent to enter relief is not slander.
translations.idiomatic: As for his failure to follow Wu Xian's advice, which led to defeat, contemporaries spoke thus chiefly because they regretted Wang Zhongze's death. That Wu Xian had no real intent to march in relief was not slander.

sentences.zh: 紇石烈牙吾塔

translations.literal: Geshilie Yawuta
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Yawuta

sentences.zh: 紇石烈牙吾塔，一名志。

translations.literal: Geshilie Yawuta, one name Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Geshilie Yawuta, also named Zhi.

sentences.zh: 本出親軍，性剛悍喜戰。

translations.literal: Originally from the personal guard army, fierce and fond of battle.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the personal guard army and was fierce and fond of battle.

sentences.zh: 貞祐間，僕散安貞為山東路宣撫使，以牙吾塔為軍中提控。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyou period Pusan Anzhen was Shandong Circuit pacification commissioner and made Yawuta army controller in the force.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenyou period Pusan Anzhen was pacification commissioner of the Shandong circuit and made Yawuta army controller in his force.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東群盜蜂起，安貞遣牙吾塔破巨蒙等四堌，又破馬耳山砦，殺劉二祖賊党四千餘人，降賊八千，虜其偽宣差程寬、招軍大使程福，又降脅從民三萬餘人。

translations.literal: At the time Shandong bandits rose in swarms; Anzhen sent Yawuta to break four stockades including Jumeng and Ma'er Mountain stockade, killed more than four thousand of Liu Erzu's band, surrendered eight thousand bandits, captured false Commissioner Cheng Kuan and Recruiting Envoy Cheng Fu, and also reduced more than thirty thousand coerced people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits swarmed across Shandong. Anzhen sent Yawuta to break four stockades including Jumeng and the Ma'er Mountain fort, killed more than four thousand of Liu Erzu's followers, accepted the surrender of eight thousand bandits, captured the false commissioner Cheng Kuan and recruiting envoy Cheng Fu, and also won over more than thirty thousand coerced civilians.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年六月，積功累遷欄通渡經略使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourth year of Zhenyou, accumulated merit promoted him repeatedly to Lan'tong Crossing strategic commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Zhenyou 4, through accumulated merit he was promoted to strategic commissioner at Lan'tong Crossing.

sentences.zh: 十月，為元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was marshal left supervising army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he became left supervising marshal.

sentences.zh: 十二月，行山東西路兵馬都總管府事，兼武甯軍節度使、徐州管內觀察使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he conducted Shandong West and East Circuit combined armies commander-in-chief affairs, also Military Pacification Army military commissioner and Xuzhou circuit observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he acted as commander-in-chief of the Shandong West and East circuits, and also held the posts of military commissioner of the Military Pacification Army and observation commissioner within Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 興定二年正月，宋兵萬餘攻泗州，牙吾塔赴援，至臨淮，遇宋人三百，掩殺殆盡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xingding Song troops numbering more than ten thousand attacked Sizhou; Yawuta went to relieve, reached Linhuai, met three hundred Song men, and in a surprise attack killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xingding 2 more than ten thousand Song troops attacked Sizhou. Yawuta marched to relieve them. At Linhuai he met three hundred Song soldiers and in a surprise attack killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 及泗州，宋兵八千圍甚急，督眾進戰，大破之，溺水死者甚眾，獲馬三百餘匹，俘五十餘人。

translations.literal: When he reached Sizhou, eight thousand Song troops besieged very urgently; he urged the masses to advance and fight, greatly defeated them, many drowned, seized more than three hundred horses, and captured more than fifty men.
translations.idiomatic: At Sizhou eight thousand Song troops had pressed the siege hard. He drove his men forward, routed them, and many drowned. He took more than three hundred horses and more than fifty prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又圍盱眙，宋人閉門堅守，不敢出。

translations.literal: He again besieged Xuyi; Song men shut the gates and held firm, not daring to come out.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Xuyi. The Song shut the gates and held firm, not daring to come out.

sentences.zh: 以騎兵分掠境內，而時遣羸卒薄城誘之。

translations.literal: With cavalry he divided to plunder within the borders, and from time to time sent weak soldiers close to the city to entice them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent cavalry to raid the countryside and from time to time sent weak detachments close to the walls to lure them out.

sentences.zh: 宋人出騎數百來拒，牙吾塔麾兵佯北，發伏擊之，斬首二百。

translations.literal: Song men came out with several hundred horsemen to resist; Yawuta commanded troops to feign retreat north, sprang ambush and struck them, beheading two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Song horsemen came out to resist. Yawuta feigned a northward retreat, sprang an ambush, and beheaded two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 宋人複出步騎八千來援，合擊敗之，殺一太尉，斬首三百。

translations.literal: Song men again came out with eight thousand foot and horse to relieve; jointly striking, he defeated them, killed one Grand Guardian, and beheaded three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent out eight thousand foot and horse in relief. He struck jointly and defeated them, killed one grand guardian, and beheaded three hundred.

sentences.zh: 尋獲覘者，稱青平宋兵甚眾，將救盱眙。

translations.literal: Soon he captured scouts who said Qingping Song troops were very numerous and would rescue Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he captured scouts who reported that a large Song force at Qingping was coming to relieve Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔移兵赴之，宋兵步騎七千人突出，兵少卻，旋以輕騎扼其後。

translations.literal: Yawuta shifted troops to go there; Song foot and horse seven thousand men burst forth; his troops being few drew back, then with light cavalry blocked their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta shifted his force to meet them. Seven thousand Song foot and horse burst forth. His force being smaller, he drew back, then sent light cavalry to block their rear.

sentences.zh: 初逗留不與戰，縱之走東南，薄諸河，斬首千餘，溺死者無算，獲馬牛數百，甲仗以千計。

translations.literal: At first he lingered and did not fight, let them flee southeast, pressed them to the rivers, beheaded more than a thousand, drowned beyond counting, seized several hundred horses and cattle, and armor and weapons by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first he held back and did not engage, let them flee southeast, and drove them to the rivers. He beheaded more than a thousand; the drowned were beyond counting. He seized several hundred horses and cattle and armor and weapons by the thousand.

sentences.zh: 師還，遇宋兵三千于連塘村，斬首千餘級，俘五十人，獲馬三十五疋，宣宗以其有功，賜金帶一。

translations.literal: The army returned and met three thousand Song troops at Liantang Village, beheaded more than a thousand, captured fifty men, seized thirty-five horses; the Xuanzong for his merit bestowed one gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he met three thousand Song troops at Liantang Village, beheaded more than a thousand, took fifty prisoners and thirty-five horses. The Xuanzong rewarded his merit with a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，敗宋人於濠州之香山村。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he defeated Song men at Xiangshan Village of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3 he defeated the Song at Xiangshan Village in Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，又敗之於滁州，斬首千級。

translations.literal: In the second month he again defeated them at Chuzhou, beheading a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he defeated them again at Chuzhou and beheaded a thousand.

sentences.zh: 拔小江寨，殺統制王大篷等，斬三萬，俘萬餘人。

translations.literal: He took Xiaojiang stockade, killed Controller Wang Dapeng and others, beheaded thirty thousand, captured more than ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He took Xiaojiang stockade, killed the controller Wang Dapeng and others, beheaded thirty thousand, and took more than ten thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 又拔輔嘉平山寨，斬首數千，俘五百餘人，獲馬牛數百，糧萬斛。

translations.literal: He again took Fujia Pingshan stockade, beheaded several thousand, captured more than five hundred men, seized several hundred horses and cattle, and ten thousand hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Fujia Pingshan stockade, beheaded several thousand, took more than five hundred prisoners, seized several hundred horses and cattle, and ten thousand hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 三月，提控奧敦吾里不大敗宋人於上津縣，兵還至濠州，宋人以軍八千拒戰，牙吾塔迎擊敗之，獲馬百餘疋。

translations.literal: In the third month Army Controller Aodun Wulida greatly defeated Song men at Shangjin County; the army returned to Haozhou, Song men with eight thousand troops resisted in battle, Yawuta met and struck and defeated them, seizing more than a hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month army controller Aodun Wulida routed the Song at Shangjin County. When the army returned to Haozhou, eight thousand Song troops resisted. Yawuta met them and defeated them, taking more than a hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，上以紅襖賊助宋為害，邊兵久勞苦，詔牙吾塔遺宋人書求戰，略曰：「宋與我國通好，百年於此，頃歲以來，納我叛亡，絕我貢幣，又遣紅襖賊乘間竊出，跳樑邊疆，使吾民不得休息。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 5, the emperor, because the Red Jacket rebels were aiding Song to cause harm and border troops had long suffered hardship, ordered Yawuta to send the Song a letter challenging battle, in summary saying: "Song and our state have been on friendly terms for a hundred years now; in recent years you have harbored our deserters, cut off our tribute goods, and moreover sent Red Jacket rebels to slip out whenever they found an opening, leaping about the frontier so that our people cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 5, because the Red Jacket rebels were helping Song harm the frontier and border troops had long been worn down, the emperor ordered Yawuta to send the Song a letter calling for battle. It read in part: "Song and our state have been at peace for a hundred years, yet in recent years you have taken in our deserters, cut off our tribute payments, and sent Red Jacket rebels to slip through whenever they saw a chance, raiding the border so our people cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 彼國若以此曹為足恃，請悉眾而來，一決勝負，果能當我之鋒，沿邊城邑當以相奉。

translations.literal: If your state thinks such men are enough to rely on, bring out your full force and come—let us settle victory and defeat in one clash; if you can truly withstand our edge, the frontier cities shall be yours for the taking.
translations.idiomatic: If your state thinks such men are enough to rely on, bring your full army and let us settle the matter in one battle. If you can truly stand against our edge, the frontier towns shall be yours.

sentences.zh: 度不能，即宜安分保境，何必狐號鼠竊、乘陰伺夜以為此態耶？

translations.literal: If you judge you cannot, then you ought to keep to your boundaries in peace—why must you yelp like foxes and steal like rats, watching for dark nights to play such a part?
translations.idiomatic: If you know you cannot, keep to your borders in peace. Why yelp like foxes and steal like rats, waiting for night to play this game?

sentences.zh: 且彼之將帥亦自受鉞總戎，而臨敵則望風遠遁，被攻則閉壘深藏，逮吾師還，然後現形耀影以示武。

translations.literal: Moreover your generals themselves receive the axe and take supreme command, yet facing the enemy they flee at a glimpse of wind; when attacked they shut the ramparts and hide deep; only after our armies return do they show their forms and flash their shadows to display martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: Your own generals receive the commander's axe and take overall command, yet at the sight of the enemy they flee far off; when attacked they shut the ramparts and hide away, and only after our armies withdraw do they show themselves and cast shadows to display martial prowess.

sentences.zh: 夫小民尚氣，女子有志者猶不爾也，切為彼國羞之。」

translations.literal: Even common folk still cherish honor; women with spirit would not act thus—we earnestly feel shame for your state on this."
translations.idiomatic: Even common folk still care about honor, and spirited women would not act this way. We are truly ashamed for your state."

sentences.zh: 先是，宋將時青襲破泗州西城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song general Shi Qing had stormed and taken Sizhou's western city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Song general Shi Qing had raided and taken the western quarter of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 二月，牙吾塔將兵取之，宋兵拒守甚力，乃募死士以梯沖並進，大敗宋兵。

translations.literal: In the second month Yawuta led troops to retake it; Song troops resisted fiercely, so he recruited dare-to-die men and advanced ladders and battering rams together, routing the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Yawuta led troops to retake it. The Song defenders fought hard, so he recruited dare-to-die men and advanced scaling ladders and battering rams together, routing the Song army.

sentences.zh: 時青乘城指麾，射中其目，遂拔眾南奔。

translations.literal: Shi Qing stood on the wall commanding; a shot struck Yawuta in the eye, whereupon Shi Qing withdrew his force south in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Qing stood on the wall directing the defense. A shot struck Yawuta in the eye, and Shi Qing then withdrew his force south in flight.

sentences.zh: 乃陳兵橫絕走路擊之，宋兵大潰，遂複泗州西城。

translations.literal: Yawuta then arrayed troops across the road to strike them; the Song army broke in great rout, and he recovered Sizhou's western city.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrayed troops across the road to cut them off and strike. The Song army broke in rout, and he recovered the western quarter of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，複出兵宋境，以報其役，破團山、賈家等諸寨，進逼濠州。

translations.literal: In the third month he again led troops into Song territory to repay the campaign, broke Tuan Mountain, Jiajia, and other stockades, and pressed close to Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he again led troops into Song territory to answer that campaign, broke the stockades at Tuan Mountain, Jiajia, and elsewhere, and pressed toward Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔慮州人出拒，躬率勁兵逆之，遇邏騎二百於城東，擊殺過半。

translations.literal: Yawuta feared the prefectural people would come out to resist and personally led crack troops to meet them; he encountered two hundred patrol horsemen east of the city and killed more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the prefectural forces would come out to resist, Yawuta personally led crack troops to meet them. East of the city he met two hundred patrol horsemen and killed more than half.

sentences.zh: 會偵者言前路芻糧甚艱，乃西掠定遠，由渦口而還。

translations.literal: When scouts reported that fodder and grain ahead were very scarce, he turned west to raid Dingyuan and returned by the Wo estuary.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts reported that fodder and grain ahead were very scarce, he turned west to raid Dingyuan and returned by the Wo estuary.

sentences.zh: 九月，又率兵渡淮，大破宋兵於團山，詔遷官升職有差。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he again led troops across the Huai, heavily defeated Song troops at Tuan Mountain, and an edict promoted officers and ranks by degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he again led troops across the Huai and routed the Song at Tuan Mountain. An edict promoted officers and raised ranks by degree.

sentences.zh: 二年四月，上言：「賞罰國之大信，帝王所以勸善而懲惡，其令一出，不可中變。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of year 2 he submitted a memorial: "Rewards and punishments are the great trust of a state; emperors use them to encourage good and punish evil—once the order goes out it must not be changed midway.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of year 2 he submitted a memorial: "Rewards and punishments are a state's greatest pledge. Emperors use them to encourage good and punish evil. Once an order is issued, it must not be altered midway.

sentences.zh: 向官軍戰歿者皆廩給其家，恩至厚也。

translations.literal: Hitherto families of officers and soldiers who died in battle have all been provisioned from the granaries—kindness reaching the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Until now the families of officers and soldiers who died in battle have all been supported from the granaries—kindness carried to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 臣近抵宿州，乃知例以楮幣折支，往往不給，至於失所。

translations.literal: When I recently reached Suzhou I learned that by regulation they are paid in paper notes at a discount, and often not paid at all, so that families lose their support.
translations.idiomatic: When I recently reached Suzhou I learned that by regulation they are paid in discounted paper notes, and often not paid at all, so that families lose their livelihood.

sentences.zh: 此殆有司出納之吝，不能奉行朝廷德意之過也。

translations.literal: This is probably the fault of officials being stingy at receipt and disbursement, unable to carry out the court's benevolent intent.
translations.idiomatic: This is probably the fault of officials being stingy in disbursement and failing to carry out the court's benevolent intent.

sentences.zh: 自今願支本色，令得贍濟。」

translations.literal: From now on I wish actual goods paid out so that they may be supported."
translations.idiomatic: From now on I ask that payments be made in kind so that families may be supported."

sentences.zh: 以糧儲方艱，詔有司給其半。

translations.literal: Because grain stores were then straitened, an edict ordered the offices to pay half.
translations.idiomatic: Because grain stores were then strained, an edict ordered the offices to pay half.

sentences.zh: 紅襖賊寇壽、潁，剽掠數日而去。

translations.literal: Red Jacket rebels raided Shou and Ying, plundered several days, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Red Jacket rebels raided Shou and Ying, plundered for several days, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔聞之，率兵渡淮，偵知硃村、孝義村有賊各數百，分兵攻之，連破兩柵，及焚其村塢數十。

translations.literal: When Yawuta heard, he led troops across the Huai; scouts learned that Zhucun and Xiaoyi villages each had several hundred rebels; he divided his force to attack, broke two palisades in succession, and burned several tens of their village forts.
translations.idiomatic: When Yawuta heard, he led troops across the Huai. Scouts reported several hundred rebels each at Zhucun and Xiaoyi villages. He divided his force to attack, broke two palisades in succession, and burned several dozen of their village forts.

sentences.zh: 還遇宋兵數百，陣淮南岸，擊殺其半，尋有兵千余自東南來追，複大敗之。

translations.literal: On his return he met several hundred Song troops arrayed on the Huai's south bank and killed half of them; soon more than a thousand troops came pursuing from the southeast and he again defeated them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he met several hundred Song troops arrayed on the south bank of the Huai and killed half of them. Soon more than a thousand troops pursued from the southeast, and he defeated them again.

sentences.zh: 先是，納合六哥殺元帥蒙古綱，據邳州以叛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Nahan Liuge had killed marshal Mengu Gang, seized Pizhou, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Nahan Liuge had killed Marshal Mengu Gang, seized Pizhou, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 十月，牙吾塔圍之，焚其樓櫓，斬首百餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Yawuta besieged it, burned its towers and stockadeworks, and beheaded more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Yawuta besieged it, burned its towers and stockadeworks, and beheaded more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋鈐轄高顯、統制侯進、正將陳榮等知不能守，共誅六哥，持其首縋城降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Song Commander Gao Xian, Controller Hou Jin, regular general Chen Rong, and others, knowing they could not hold, jointly killed Liuge, lowered his head by rope from the wall, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Song commander Gao Xian, controller Hou Jin, regular general Chen Rong, and others, knowing they could not hold, jointly killed Liuge, lowered his head by rope from the wall, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 六哥既誅，眾猶拒守，方督兵進攻，宋總領劉斌、提控黃溫等縛首亂顏俊、戚誼、完顏乞哥，及梟提控金山八打首，遣其校馬俊、吳珪來獻。

translations.literal: After Liuge was killed the masses still resisted; as he was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others bound the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, sending their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.
translations.idiomatic: After Liuge was killed the people still resisted. As Yawuta was pressing the assault, Song chief Liu Bin, superintendent Huang Wen, and others sent the heads of the rebels Luan Yanjun, Qi Yi, and Wanyan Qige, and displayed the head of superintendent Jinshan Bada, dispatching their adjutants Ma Jun and Wu Gui to present them.

sentences.zh: 既而紅襖監軍徐福、統制王喜等亦遣其總領孫成、總押徐琦納款。

translations.literal: Then Red Jacket monitor Xu Fu, Controller Wang Xi, and others also sent their chief Sun Cheng and superintendent Xu Qi to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Then Red Jacket monitor Xu Fu, controller Wang Xi, and others also sent their chief Sun Cheng and superintendent Xu Qi to submit allegiance.

sentences.zh: 劉斌等遂率軍民出降，牙吾塔入城，撫慰其眾，各使安集，又招獲紅襖統制十有五人，將官訓練百三十有九人。

translations.literal: Liu Bin and the rest then led soldiers and civilians out to surrender; Yawuta entered the city, comforted the masses, had each settle in peace, and further recruited fifteen Red Jacket controllers and one hundred thirty-nine officers and trainers.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin and the rest then led soldiers and civilians out to surrender. Yawuta entered the city, comforted the people, and had each group settle in peace. He also recruited fifteen Red Jacket controllers and one hundred thirty-nine officers and trainers.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣人來報，仍函六哥首以獻。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent men to report and still boxed Liuge's head to present.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent men to report and still sent Liuge's head in a box as tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣宗大喜，進牙吾塔官一階，賜金三百兩、內府重幣十端，將士遷賞有差。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong rejoiced greatly, promoted Yawuta one rank, bestowed three hundred taels of gold and ten bolts of imperial fine silks, and rewarded officers and soldiers with promotions by degree.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong rejoiced greatly, promoted Yawuta one rank, bestowed three hundred taels of gold and ten bolts of imperial fine silks, and rewarded officers and soldiers with promotions by degree.

sentences.zh: 正大三年十一月，北兵猝入西夏，攻中興府甚急。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of Zhengda year 3 northern troops suddenly entered Western Xia and pressed Zhongxing Prefecture fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Zhengda year 3, northern troops suddenly entered Western Xia and pressed Zhongxing Prefecture fiercely.

sentences.zh: 召陝西行省及陝州、靈寶二總帥訛可、牙吾塔議兵。

translations.literal: The Shaanxi branch secretariat and the two marshals of Shanzhou and Lingbao, Wanyan Eke and Yawuta, were summoned to deliberate on troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi branch secretariat and the two marshals of Shanzhou and Lingbao, Wanyan Eke and Yawuta, were summoned to discuss military measures.

sentences.zh: 又詔諭兩省曰：「倘邊方有警，內地可憂，若不早圖，恐成噬臍。

translations.literal: An edict also instructed the two secretariats: "If the frontier should have alarm, the interior may be at risk; if we do not plan early, we may come to bite our navel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also instructed the two secretariats: "If the frontier should raise an alarm, the interior may be at risk. If we do not plan early, we may come to bite our navel.

sentences.zh: 旦夕事勢不同，隨機應變，若逐旋申奏，恐失事機，並從行省從宜規畫。」

translations.literal: Day and night the situation differs—respond opportunely as events change; if we report step by step we may lose the moment—all follow the branch secretariat in discretionary planning."
translations.idiomatic: Day and night the situation differs; respond as events require. If we report step by step we may lose the moment. All follow the branch secretariat in discretionary planning."

sentences.zh: 四年，牙吾塔複取平陽，獲馬三千。

translations.literal: In year 4 Yawuta again took Pingyang and captured three thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Yawuta again took Pingyang and captured three thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 是歲，大兵既滅夏國，進攻陝西德順、秦州、清水等城、遂自鳳翔入京兆，關中大震。

translations.literal: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed Xia, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang; Guanzhong shook greatly.
translations.idiomatic: That year, after Great Yuan forces had destroyed the Xia state, they attacked Dexun, Qinzhou, Qingshui, and other cities in Shaanxi, then entered Jingzhao from Fengxiang. Guanzhong was shaken to its core.

sentences.zh: 五年，圍慶陽。

translations.literal: In year 5 they besieged Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 they besieged Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，上命陝省以羊酒及幣赴慶陽犒北帥，為緩師計。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of year 6 the emperor ordered the Shaanxi secretariat to take sheep, wine, and silks to Qingyang to reward the northern commanders as a strategy to delay the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 6 the emperor ordered the Shaanxi secretariat to take sheep, wine, and silks to Qingyang to reward the northern commanders as a strategy to slow the campaign.

sentences.zh: 北中亦遣唐慶等往來議和，尋遣斡骨欒為小使，徑來行省。

translations.literal: The north also sent Tang Qing and others back and forth to discuss peace; soon they dispatched Woguluan as a junior envoy directly to the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The north also sent Tang Qing and others back and forth to discuss peace. Soon they dispatched Woguluan as a junior envoy directly to the branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔以牙吾塔與副樞蒲阿權簽樞密院事，內族訛可將兵救慶陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta with Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs; imperial clansman Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month an edict appointed Yawuta and Vice Censor-in-Chief Pu'a to hold acting signatures at the Bureau of Military Affairs, while imperial clansman Wanyan Eke was to lead troops to relieve Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，戰于大昌原，慶陽圍解。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 7 they fought at Dachangyuan and the siege of Qingyang was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 7 they fought at Dachangyuan and the siege of Qingyang was lifted.

sentences.zh: 詔以牙吾塔為左副元帥，屯京兆。

translations.literal: An edict made Yawuta Left Vice Marshal and stationed him at Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yawuta Left Vice Marshal and stationed him at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 初，斡骨欒來，行省恐泄事機，因留之。

translations.literal: When Woguluan had first come, the branch secretariat feared leaking the situation and therefore detained him.
translations.idiomatic: When Woguluan had first arrived, the branch secretariat feared leaking their plans and therefore detained him.

sentences.zh: 蒲阿等既解慶陽之圍，志氣驕滿，乃遣還，謂使者曰：「我已準備軍馬，可戰鬥來。」

translations.literal: After Pu'a and the others had lifted the siege of Qingyang, their morale was swollen with pride; they sent him back, telling the envoy: "We have already prepared horses and troops—come fight if you will."
translations.idiomatic: After Pu'a and the others had lifted the siege of Qingyang, their spirits were swollen with pride. They sent Woguluan back, telling the envoy: "We have already prepared horses and troops. Come fight if you will."

sentences.zh: 語甚不遜，斡骨欒以此言上聞，太宗皇帝大怒，至應州，以九日拜天，即親統大兵入陝西。

translations.literal: The words were very insolent; Woguluan reported this speech upward; Emperor Taizong was greatly enraged; reaching Yingzhou, on the ninth day he worshipped Heaven and at once personally led great forces into Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: The words were deeply insolent. Woguluan reported them upward. Emperor Taizong was greatly enraged. Reaching Yingzhou, on the ninth day he worshipped Heaven and at once personally led great forces into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷居民于河南，棄京兆東還。

translations.literal: In year 8 the inhabitants were moved to Henan; Jingzhao was abandoned and they withdrew east.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 the inhabitants were moved to Henan. Jingzhao was abandoned and they withdrew east.

sentences.zh: 五月，至閿鄉，得寒疾，汗不出，死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, reaching Wenxiang, he contracted a chilling malady and could not sweat, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, reaching Wenxiang, he contracted a chilling illness, could not sweat, and died.

sentences.zh: 「塔」亦作「太」，亦曰「牙忽帶」，蓋女直語，無正字也。

translations.literal: "Ta" is also written "Tai"; it is also called "Yahudai"—a Jurchen word with no standard characters.
translations.idiomatic: "Ta" is also written "Tai"; it is also called "Yahudai"—a Jurchen word with no standard written form.

sentences.zh: 是歲九月，國信使內族乘慶自北使還，始知牙吾塔不遜激怒之語，且言慶等在旁心魄震盪，殆不忍聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year credential envoy imperial clansman Cheng Qing returned from the northern mission and first learned of Yawuta's insolent words that had enraged them; he also said that while Qing was at their side his heart and soul shook, scarcely able to bear hearing it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year the credential envoy, imperial clansman Cheng Qing, returned from the northern mission and first learned of Yawuta's insolent words that had provoked them. He also said that while he stood at their side his heart and soul shook, scarcely able to bear what he heard.

sentences.zh: 當時以帥臣不知書，誤國乃爾。

translations.literal: At the time it was said that because the commander did not understand letters, he had thus mistaken the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people said that because the commander was illiterate, he had mistaken the state in this way.

sentences.zh: 塔為人鷙狠狼戾，好結小人，不聽朝廷節制。

translations.literal: Yawuta as a man was fierce, cruel, and wolfish, fond of bonding with petty men, not listening to court regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta was fierce, cruel, and wolfish by nature. He liked to bond with petty men and would not obey court regulation.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝，詣省堂，詆毀宰執，宰執亦不敢言，而上倚其鎮東方，亦優容之。

translations.literal: Once he came to court and went to the Secretariat hall, slandering the chief ministers; the chief ministers also did not dare speak, while the emperor relied on him to guard the east and likewise indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came to court and went to the Secretariat hall to slander the chief ministers. The chief ministers did not dare reply, while the emperor relied on him to guard the east and likewise indulged him.

sentences.zh: 尤不喜文士，僚屬有長裾者，輒以刀截去。

translations.literal: He especially disliked literary gentlemen; if subordinates wore long robes he would slash them off with a blade.
translations.idiomatic: He especially disliked literary gentlemen. If a subordinate wore long robes, he would slash them off with a blade.

sentences.zh: 又喜淩侮使者，凡朝廷遣使來，必以酒食困之。

translations.literal: He also delighted in humiliating envoys; whenever the court sent an envoy he would trouble him with food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: He also delighted in humiliating envoys. Whenever the court sent an envoy, he would wear him down with food and drink.

sentences.zh: 或辭以不飲，因並食不給，使餓而去。

translations.literal: If they declined saying they would not drink, he would give no food at all and send them away hungry.
translations.idiomatic: If they declined to drink, he would give no food at all and send them away hungry.

sentences.zh: 司農少卿張用章以行戶部過宿，塔飲以酒。

translations.literal: Minister of Agriculture Vice Minister Zhang Yongzhang was passing through on a Households mission and stayed overnight; Yawuta made him drink wine.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Agriculture Zhang Yongzhang was passing through on a Households mission and stayed overnight. Yawuta pressed wine on him.

sentences.zh: 張辭以寒疾，塔笑曰：「此易治耳。」

translations.literal: Zhang declined on account of a chilling illness; Yawuta laughed and said, "That is easy to cure."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang declined on account of a chilling illness. Yawuta laughed and said, "That is easy to cure."

sentences.zh: 趨左右持艾來，臥張於床，灸之數十。

translations.literal: He hurried his attendants to bring moxa, laid Zhang on the bed, and moxa-burned him several tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried his attendants to bring moxa, laid Zhang on the bed, and burned him with moxa several dozen times.

sentences.zh: 又以銀符佩妓，屢往州郡取賕 ，州將之妻皆遠迎迓，號「省差行首」，厚賄之。

translations.literal: He also wore a silver tally to courtesans and repeatedly went to prefectures and districts to take bribes; wives of prefectural commanders all went far to meet and escort, calling them "provincial detachment headmen," and gave them heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He also wore a silver tally on courtesans and repeatedly went to prefectures and districts to take bribes. Wives of prefectural commanders went far to meet and escort them, calling them "provincial detachment headmen," and gave them heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 禦史康錫上章劾之，且曰：「朝廷容之，適所以害之。

translations.literal: Censor Kang Xi submitted a memorial impeaching him, saying: "The court's indulgence of him is precisely what harms him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Kang Xi submitted a memorial impeaching him, saying: "The court's indulgence of him is precisely what harms him.

sentences.zh: 欲保全其人，宜加裁制。」

translations.literal: If one wishes to preserve the man, one should add restraint."
translations.idiomatic: If one wishes to preserve the man, one should impose restraint."

sentences.zh: 朝廷竟不治其罪，以屢敗宋兵，威震淮、泗。

translations.literal: The court ultimately did not punish his crimes; because he repeatedly defeated Song troops, his prestige shook Huai and Si.
translations.idiomatic: The court ultimately did not punish his crimes. Because he repeatedly defeated Song troops, his prestige shook the Huai and Si region.

sentences.zh: 好用鼓椎擊人，世呼曰「盧鼓椎」，其名可以怖兒啼，大概如呼「麻胡」雲。

translations.literal: He liked to beat people with a drum mallet; the world called him "Lu drum mallet," a name that could frighten children's crying—much like calling "Mahu," as they say.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to beat people with a drum mallet. The world called him "Lu drum mallet," a name that could frighten children into silence—much like crying "Mahu," as people say.

sentences.zh: 有子名阿里合，世目曰「小鼓椎」，嘗為元帥，從哀宗至歸德，與蒲察官奴作亂，伏誅。

translations.literal: He had a son named Alihe, called by the world "Little drum mallet"; he once was marshal, followed Emperor Aizong to Guide, joined Pucha Guannu in rebellion, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son named Alihe, known to the world as "Little drum mallet." He once served as marshal, followed Emperor Aizong to Guide, joined Pucha Guannu in rebellion, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：金自胡沙虎、高琪用事，風俗一變，朝廷矯寬厚之政，好為苛察，然為之不果，反成姑息。

translations.literal: The encomium says: From the time Hushahu and Gao Qi held power in Jin, customs changed at a stroke; the court narrowed the policy of generous forbearance and came to like harsh scrutiny, yet could not carry it through and instead became indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: From the time Hushahu and Gao Qi held power in Jin, customs changed at a stroke. The court narrowed its generous policy and came to favor harsh scrutiny, yet could not carry it through and instead became indulgent.

sentences.zh: 將帥鄙儒雅之風，好為粗豪，然用非其宜，終至跋扈。

translations.literal: Generals despised refined elegance and liked crude bravado, yet employed them inappropriately and in the end came to insubordination.
translations.idiomatic: Generals despised refined manners and favored crude bravado, yet employed them inappropriately and in the end came to insubordination.

sentences.zh: 牙吾塔戰勝攻取，威行江、淮，而矜暴不法，肆侮王人，此豈可制者乎？

translations.literal: Yawuta in victory attacked and took; his might ran the Yangtze and Huai, yet he was violent and lawless, wantonly insulting the king's men—could such a one be controlled?
translations.idiomatic: Yawuta won battles and took cities; his might ran the Yangtze and Huai, yet he was violent and lawless and wantonly insulted the king's men. Could such a man be controlled?

sentences.zh: 棄陝而歸，死於道途，殆其幸歟！

translations.literal: Abandoning Shaanxi and returning, he died on the road—perhaps it was his good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning Shaanxi and returning east, he died on the road—perhaps that was his good fortune!

sentences.zh: 其子效尤，竟陷大僇，君子乃知康錫之言不為過也。

translations.literal: His son imitated him and in the end fell to great punishment; gentlemen then knew that Kang Xi's words had not been excessive.
translations.idiomatic: His son followed his example and in the end suffered great punishment. Gentlemen then knew that Kang Xi's words had not been excessive.
